headline: The deepest novel signal is that an undocumented (blank) discontinuation reason on the PRIOR line triples the odds of a COTA over-split (OR 3.24, 32% vs 13%) — a distinct, line-independent failure mode that is mechanically separate from the dominant but already-known identical-drug-set artifact.

ranked_findings.title: Blank prior-line discontinuation reason triples over-split odds (previous-row attribution)
ranked_findings.one_liner: Over-splits cluster where the prior line ended with NO coded reason: 32.4% (24/74) vs 12.9% (91/706), Fisher OR=3.24 (95% CI 1.84-5.49), p=4.2e-5; current-row attribution is null (p=0.22).
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: A genuinely new, line-independent failure mode (COTA over-splits where there is no documented clinical event to anchor the line change) that is largely orthogonal to the known drug-drop pattern; the previous-vs-current row attribution flip is the novel methodological contribution.

ranked_findings.title: Identical-drug-set / bracket-phase formatting artifact dominates over-split volume
ranked_findings.one_liner: Current row identical drug set to prior = 40.5% (30/74) vs 1.7% (12/706), OR=39.4, p=2.1e-24, line-adjusted OR 25-39; 21/30 differ only in bracket-phase count.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Highest-yield single fix target with a concrete root cause: COTA's line logic fires on regimen-string phase formatting, not actual drug changes. Extends the known same_exact_regimen_repeated label with a control-based effect size and the phase mechanism.

ranked_findings.title: PI+Steroids regimens are specifically protected (only Bonferroni-surviving family)
ranked_findings.one_liner: Opportunity-normalized 4.2% (12/284) vs 12.5% (62/496), OR=0.31, p=1.1e-4; only 1 of 36 families passes Bonferroni; survives line and exact-repeat adjustment (OR 0.40); PI-specific not a generic steroid-doublet effect.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Inverts the assigned high-rate hypothesis (which is null) and is the single finding surviving strict multiplicity control; identifies a regimen class COTA handles correctly, pointing at stable maintenance/continuation as the protective mechanism.

ranked_findings.title: Severe over-counting is repeat-offender accumulation of atomic +1 events, never a big jump
ranked_findings.one_liner: All 74/74 over-splits are exactly +1 (doc_inc=0); cumulative +2..+5 = a patient accumulating multiple separate +1s (per-patient max shift = over-split count for all 52 offenders). Repeat offenders have more TRUE lines (median 9 vs 6, p=0.008).
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Establishes the corrected-LOT rule (don't increment on doctor-hold rows) and shows severity is opportunity, not a distinct driver. Part 2 (independent line-burden effect) is refuted by endogeneity: using COTA's inflated line total; vanishes on doctor totals (p 4.6e-6 to 0.16).

ranked_findings.title: Multi-phase PREVIOUS regimen at relapse predicts over-splits but is mostly confounded by same-set
ranked_findings.one_liner: Relapsed prev-multiphase 19.7% vs 4.9% (OR 4.75, p=9.5e-8) and survives de-escalation removal (OR 4.08, p=4.8e-5); BUT marginal effect collapses to OR 1.12 once identical-drug-set is in the model and is null among non-same-set (OR 1.39, p=0.30).
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Mostly a downstream correlate of the identical-drug-set artifact (multi-phase prior lines tend to be followed by a row repeating the induction set); a residual independent effect survives only in the narrow relapsed non-de-escalation slice. Report as qualified, not a standalone driver.

ranked_findings.title: COTA LOT is a contiguous row index; over-splitting is one-directional by construction
ranked_findings.one_liner: cota seq=1..n for all 136 patients, cota_inc identical +1, doc_inc in {0,1}, crosstab exactly (0,1):74/(1,1):706, binomial p=5.3e-23; closed form shift = baseline_offset + running doctor-holds; lone -3 patient is baseline left-censoring.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Pins the structural root cause (merges are unrepresentable) and yields the closed-form corrected-LOT rule; flags a real blind spot (the flag cannot detect baseline left-censoring offsets for mid-treatment entrants).

ranked_findings.title: Decay curve is a genuine declining hazard, monotone, not quadratic
ranked_findings.one_liner: Per-transition hazard declines (Spearman -0.80, p=0.010); doctor-line trend OR=0.784 (p=0.004) is steeper than COTA-line OR=0.849, so NOT an x-axis artifact; quadratic 'U-shape' is a 3-event tail artifact (quad LR p 0.034 to 0.63 when trimmed).
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the known decay is real hazard not survivorship and corrects the 'quadratic' eyeballing; power-law vs exponential indistinguishable so claim limited to monotone decay. L11+ ~0% facts are survivorship-empty.

ranked_findings.title: Transition TYPE dominates line; exact-repeat flat and high-yield
ranked_findings.one_liner: Type x over-split chi2=263 (ORs 109/26/8) vs line OR=0.98 after type control; exact-regimen-repeat over-splits at 71% (30/42) regardless of line.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Robust core of the curve-by-pattern hypothesis; reinforces that the identical-set artifact (not line number) carries the signal. The companion de-escalation 'inverted sub-curve' claim was refuted.

ranked_findings.title: Induction-to-maintenance collapse is NOT a driver (reversed)
ranked_findings.one_liner: Multi-drug to single-agent depleted in over-splits (2/74=2.7% vs 70/706=9.9%, OR 0.25); staying multi-drug (>=3) enriched (OR 2.07, p=0.005, survives line-stratified CMH); dominant maintenance agent is daratumumab not lenalidomide.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Valid null/reversal: debunks the lenalidomide-maintenance assumption and shows over-splits cluster at multi-drug reshuffles, consistent with the identical-set/same-structure patterns.

ranked_findings.title: Backbone 'swing drugs' are depleted; transplant-conditioning swing is fragile
ranked_findings.one_liner: Daratumumab/carfilzomib/pomalidomide/bortezomib all DEPLETED as swings (RR 0.07/0/0.33/0.56); transplant-added enrichment (9/74 vs 41/706, OR 2.25, p=0.044) fails LOPO, Bonferroni, and line stratification.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Refutes the prior that common backbone agents drive over-splits (valuable null); the positive transplant claim is suggestive but multiplicity-fragile and line-confounded, not an established driver.

ranked_findings.title: No patient-level super-spreader clustering beyond exposure
ranked_findings.one_liner: Exposure-conditioned dispersion ratio 0.85 (mild under-dispersion); marginal VMR 1.28 fully explained by exposure heterogeneity (bootstrap-expected 1.05 covers it); transplant patient-level OR=1.00.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Correct null: per-patient counts are binomial given exposure; the marginal Poisson signal is the mis-specified trap. Tells the team not to chase super-spreaders; severity is opportunity (rank 4).

ranked_findings.title: Line duration and inter-line gaps are essentially null
ranked_findings.one_liner: Current-line duration p=0.43, prev-line p=0.23, central gap p=0.51 all null; only a near-zero-gap tail excess (gap<=1 day OR 1.81, p=0.049) that does not survive multiple-comparison correction.
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Closes the unused date columns: over-splits are not short fragments or overlapping continuations; the lone borderline signal is noise after correction. Stop chasing timing-based explanations.

ranked_findings.title: Steroid/dexamethasone churn is a null hypothesis
ranked_findings.one_liner: Steroid-only changes = 2/74 (2.7%), dex-drop RR 1.06 (p=0.86), any-steroid-change if anything lower in over-splits (OR 0.77); the real signal found while testing is the identical-drug-set artifact (rank 2).
ranked_findings.why_it_matters: Cleanly rejects steroid churn as a driver and pivots to the identical-drug-set mechanism; valuable for telling the prof which intuitive hypothesis is empty.

raw_findings.title: Over-split-only asymmetry & the lone under-count patient

finding.claim: COTA's LOT is a literal one-per-regimen-row counter (every patient's COTA sequence is exactly 1,2,3,...,n), so its per-transition increment is ALWAYS exactly +1; the error is structurally one-directional because the only way to disagree is for the doctor to HOLD a line (doc_inc=0), which COTA can never represent — and the lone "under-count" patient is pure left-censoring, not a missed merge.
finding.evidence: Across 780 transitions, the (doc_inc, cota_inc) pair takes exactly TWO values: (0,1) 74 times = every over-split, and (1,1) 706 times = every aligned. cota_inc has a single unique value (1.0) across all 780 transitions; doc_inc is only ever 0 or 1; there are 0 transitions with cota_inc==0 (a merge) and 0 with cota_inc>1 (a multi-jump). All 136/136 patients have COTA lot sequence == 1,2,...,n exactly (no skips, repeats, or holds). Sign/binomial test on the 74 discordant transitions all pointing the over direction: p=5.3e-23. Per-patient final cota_minus_doctor_lot_shift: -3 x1, 0 x83, 1 x35, 2 x14, 3 x2, 5 x1. The ONLY negative patient (ada4c8dc) has shift=-3 already at its BASELINE row: COTA labels its first observed regimen [bortezomib,dexamethasone,lenalidomide] as line 1 while the doctor labels it line 4, and the offset stays exactly -3 across all 4 rows because every one of that patient's transitions is perfectly aligned (cota_inc=doc_inc=1). Baseline doctor_lot is 1 for 135/136 patients and 4 for this one; baseline COTA lot is 1 for all 136.
finding.effect_size: Directional asymmetry is absolute: 74 over-splits vs 0 under-splits (74/74 of all discordant transitions, 100%, one-sided). The lone negative patient is 1/136 (0.7%) and is fully explained by a constant baseline offset of -3, not by any per-transition under-count (0 of its transitions are errors).
finding.sample_size: 780 transitions (74 OVER + 706 ALIGN) over 136 patients; 136 baseline rows; lone exception subgroup n=1 patient (4 rows).
finding.caveats: The mechanism is partly tautological/data-artifact: COTA emits one row per regimen and the row counter IS the LOT, so by construction cota_inc=1 and merges are unrepresentable — this guarantees one-directionality rather than it being an empirical coincidence, but it's still the true root cause of why the error can only ever over-split. The lone exception (n=1) is left-censoring inferred from the data structure (doctor baseline=4, no prior rows in the file, diag_dt 2019 with a mature regimen); I cannot see the 3 prior lines directly, only that the offset originates at baseline and never changes. The flag did NOT miss a real under-count, but it also cannot detect baseline left-censoring offsets — a genuine blind spot of the over-split flag for any patient entering mid-treatment.
finding.method: Canonical load of All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid,_original_row_order. Defined cota_inc=cota_lot_numeric-previous_cota_lot_numeric and doc_inc=doctor_lot_numeric_for_transition-previous_doctor_lot_numeric on the 780 non-baseline rows; cross-tabulated (doc_inc,cota_inc); checked unique values and counts of cota_inc==0 / cota_inc>1. Verified each patient's COTA lot list equals range(1,n+1). Ran scipy.stats.binomtest(74,74,0.5,'greater'). For the exception: took groupby(cpid).tail(1) of cota_minus_doctor_lot_shift to find net per-patient shift (only ada4c8dc<0, value -3), then printed that patient's full row sequence and the baseline rows' cota/doctor lot numbers to confirm the offset originates at baseline and is constant.
finding.secondary_observations: Every over-split sits at a doctor HOLD (doc_inc=0), meaning the doctor judged consecutive distinct regimen rows to be the same line of therapy — consistent with the known de-escalation/drug-drop and re-expansion sub-patterns. Net-positive final shifts (1:35, 2:14, 3:2, 5:1) show errors accumulate within patients: a single patient can carry up to 5 cumulative over-counts. Because COTA's LOT equals a contiguous row index, the cumulative gap cota_minus_doctor_lot_shift is exactly the running count of doctor-holds so far minus the baseline offset — a clean closed-form, useful for building a corrected LOT by simply not incrementing on doctor-hold rows.

verdict.recomputed: Re-ran canonical load: 916 rows, 136 patients, 74 OVER / 706 ALIGN / 136 BASE. Computed cota_inc and doc_inc on the 780 transitions: cota_inc has a SINGLE unique value (1.0), doc_inc only {0,1}, zero merges (cota_inc==0) and zero multi-jumps (cota_inc>1). Crosstab(doc_inc,cota_inc) = exactly (0,1):74 and (1,1):706. All 136/136 patients have COTA sequence == range(1,n+1); further, COTA lot == within-patient 1-based row index for ALL 916 rows and line_of_therapy_c==cota_lot_numeric (confirms row-counter mechanism). scipy binomtest(74,74,0.5,'greater') p=5.29e-23. Per-patient final shift: -3×1, 0×83, 1×35, 2×14, 3×2, 5×1 (exact match). Baseline doctor_lot=1 for 135, =4 for 1 patient; baseline COTA=1 for all 136. Lone negative patient ada4c8dc: baseline offset -3, all 3 non-baseline transitions aligned (cota_inc=doc_inc=1), offset constant -3 across 4 rows. Extra checks: the 74 over-split rows are EXACTLY the 74 doctor-hold (doc_inc==0) non-baseline rows; and shift = baseline_offset + cumulative doctor-holds holds for every patient (closed form verified True).
verdict.main_confound: None found — and standard confounds (line number, family, transplant, commonness) are inapplicable because the claim is a structural counting identity (COTA LOT == contiguous row index), not a rate that could be confounded. The honest weakness is that the mechanism is partly tautological (one-directionality is guaranteed by construction, not an empirical coincidence) and the lone exception is n=1 with left-censoring inferred, not directly observed — both of which the author already states clearly.
verdict.critique: Every numeric claim reproduced exactly, including the secondary observations and the closed-form. The finding's strength is also its main caveat: the one-directional asymmetry is a data artifact of COTA emitting one row per regimen with LOT = row index, so merges are unrepresentable by construction — this is correctly flagged as 'tautological/data-artifact', so it is not over-claimed. The lone under-count patient is genuinely n=1 and left-censoring is an inference (cannot see the 3 missing prior lines), but it is well-supported (doctor baseline=4, COTA=1, constant offset, all transitions aligned) and crucially does not weaken the asymmetry claim since none of that patient's transitions are errors. The novel, useful extension beyond known facts is the verified identity that cota_minus_doctor_lot_shift = baseline_offset + running count of doctor-holds, which yields a trivial corrected-LOT rule (don't increment on doctor-hold rows). Confidence high; only humility note is the inherent n=74 / n=1 limits, already acknowledged.

raw_findings.title: Decay-curve mechanism: hazard vs survivorship, and its functional form

finding.claim: The line-number decay in COTA over-splitting is a GENUINE declining per-transition hazard (not pure survivorship), and its shape is a monotone exponential/power-law decay -- "quadratic" is an eyeballing artifact created by noisy late lines, not a real U-shape.
finding.evidence: Per-transition hazard within each line's risk set (over-splits / transitions-into-line-k): L2 19/136=0.140, L3 17/134=0.127, L4 12/127=0.094, L5 7/101=0.069, L6 6/79=0.076, L7 3/60=0.050, L8 5/46=0.109, L9 1/34=0.029, L10 1/24=0.042 (Wilson 95% CIs computed; L2 [0.091,0.208]). Genuine hazard decline: Spearman(hazard vs k, lines 2-10) rho=-0.80 p=0.0096. Survivorship ALSO operates: risk set falls 136->24 (5.67x) L2->L10 while hazard falls 3.35x; their product = the 19x raw-count drop (exp count L2=19.0, L10=1.0). Logistic is_over~k, stable range lines 2-10 (n=741): beta=-0.163, OR/line=0.849, z=-2.59, p=0.0097; full range (n=780): OR/line=0.904, z=-2.01, p=0.045. Cochran-Armitage trend z=-2.02 p=0.044. QUADRATIC IS ARTIFACT: full-range quad LR test chi2=4.48 p=0.034 BUT k^2 coef=+0.021 (U-shaped UP, driven by L14 2/4 and L16 1/2 noise); restricting to lines 2-10 the quad term vanishes (LR chi2=0.24 p=0.63). Weighted curve fits to hazard (lines 2-10, weight=risk set): power_law a=0.224 b=0.623 AIC=-30.42 (BEST), exp_decay a=0.191 r=0.159 AIC=-30.11, quadratic AIC=-28.51, linear AIC=-28.10.
finding.effect_size: Per-line multiplicative decline: OR=0.849 per line (lines 2-10), i.e. ~15% relative drop in over-split odds per additional line. Hazard ratio L2/L10=3.35x. Power-law exponent b=0.62 (h(k) approx 0.22*k^-0.62) or exp decay rate r=0.16/line.
finding.sample_size: 780 transitions (74 over-split + 706 aligned); risk sets per line L2=136 down to L10=24; functional-form fits used lines 2-10 (n>=20 per line, 9 points); stable logistic n=741.
finding.caveats: Late lines (k>=11) have tiny risk sets (<=15, several =1-4) so their hazards (incl. L14=0.50, L16=0.50) are noise; they create a spurious U-shape that fools the full-range quadratic test -- so the quadratic 'significance' is an artifact, not signal. Power-law vs exponential cannot be distinguished here (AIC within 0.3, both ~equal wR2 0.76-0.77); claim is only that the shape is monotone-decay, not specifically which. n=74 over-splits total; CIs are wide. 'Line number' = COTA's cota_lot_numeric, which is itself inflated relative to the doctor in over-split rows, so k is COTA's count not ground truth (a definitional confound for the x-axis). L8 bump (0.109) is within CI noise. No control for family/transplant confound in this trend (separate question).
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped cols, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. TRANS = 780 rows where status != baseline_first_lot_row. k=cota_lot_numeric (line the transition advances INTO); is_over=1 if status==candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split. Risk set at line k = count of transitions with that k. Hazard = mean(is_over) per k with Wilson 95% binomial CI. Trend: sklearn LogisticRegression(C=inf) of is_over~k with SE from Fisher information (Xt W X)^-1; Cochran-Armitage manual; quadratic via LR test (2*dLogLik, chi2 df=1) adding k^2, run on full range AND lines 2-10. Functional forms (linear, quadratic, a*exp(-r*k), a*k^-b) fit with scipy curve_fit on lines 2-10 weighted sigma=1/sqrt(risk set), compared by weighted R^2 and Gaussian AIC. Decomposition compares hazard ratio vs risk-set ratio L2 vs L10. Read-only.
finding.secondary_observations: The number reaching each line drops sharply: only 24 patients reach L10, 15 reach L11, <=4 by L14 -- so all "L11+ ~0%" facts are survivorship-dominated and statistically empty (cannot distinguish 0 from the L2 rate at those n). Per-line OR is noticeably steeper when you exclude the noisy tail (0.849 vs 0.904), meaning the published full-range decay slightly UNDERSTATES the true early-line decline. The single biggest contributor to total over-splits is simply that line 2 has both the highest hazard (0.140) and the largest risk set (136), making early lines (L2-L4) account for 48/74 = 65% of all over-splits.

verdict.recomputed: Re-ran everything independently from the canonical frame (780 transitions, 74 over-split). Hazard table reproduces to the decimal: L2 19/136=0.140 (Wilson [0.091,0.208]), L3 0.127, L4 0.094, L5 0.069, L6 0.076, L7 0.050, L8 0.109, L9 0.029, L10 0.042, then noisy tail L14 2/4=0.50, L16 1/2=0.50. Spearman(hazard,k | lines 2-10) rho=-0.800 p=0.0096. My own Newton logistic: stable (2-10) n=741 beta_k=-0.163, OR=0.849, z=-2.59 p=0.0097; full n=780 OR=0.904 z=-2.01 p=0.045. Cochran-Armitage full z=-2.02 p=0.044. Quadratic LR: full chi2=4.48 p=0.034 with k^2 coef=+0.0213 (U-up); restricted to 2-10 chi2=0.24 p=0.626. Functional fits (weighted, lines 2-10) AIC: power=-30.42 (a=0.224,b=0.623), exp=-30.11 (a=0.191,r=0.159), quad=-28.51, linear=-28.10. Hazard ratio L2/L10=3.35, riskset ratio 5.67, product=19x raw count. Every figure in the claim matched.
verdict.main_confound: The x-axis is COTA's own (inflated) line count in over-split rows, which the colleague honestly flags. I tested it directly: re-running the trend on the DOCTOR's ground-truth line number gives OR=0.784, z=-2.86, p=0.0042 over lines 2-10 -- steeper and more significant, so the decay is NOT an x-axis artifact. The remaining limitation is genuine smallness (74 over-splits, wide CIs) and no control for family/transplant, but that is explicitly scoped out as a separate question.
verdict.critique: The finding is unusually well-disciplined: it separates hazard from survivorship, gives the right denominators, and correctly diagnoses the quadratic "significance" as a tail artifact. I stress-tested the artifact claim by progressively trimming the tail -- the quad LR p-value goes 0.034 (full) -> 0.626 (k<=10) -> 0.933 (k<=11) and the k^2 coefficient collapses from +0.021 toward zero/negative as the 3 tail over-splits (L14x2, L16x1) are removed, confirming the U-shape is 3 events in risk sets of 2-4, not signal. Power-law vs exponential are genuinely indistinguishable (AIC within 0.3) and the claim correctly limits itself to "monotone decay." The only thing I'd push on is that with 9 points and 74 events the AIC ranking is fragile and shouldn't be over-read, but the colleague already says exactly that. Verdict: confirmed -- arithmetic is exact, control group correct, the main confound was tested and fails to explain it.

raw_findings.title: Does the decay differ by error type (de-escalation vs addition vs repeat)?

finding.claim: The over-split "decay curve" is a mixture of two oppositely-shaped sub-curves: exact-regimen-repeat over-splits are flat across line number (the true dominant driver), while de-escalation over-splits are INVERTED — zero at line 2 and rising thereafter — the opposite of the hypothesized induction-to-maintenance early peak.
finding.evidence: Classifying the 74 over-splits by drug-set relation to the prior row (current==prev=exact_repeat n=30; prev subset cur=addition n=17; cur subset prev=de_escalation n=14; other n=13). Conditional over-split risk over ALL transitions of each type: exact_repeat 30/42=71.4%, de_escalation 14/37=37.8%, addition 17/111=15.3%, other 13/590=2.2% (chi2=263.1, dof=3, p=9.4e-57). WITHIN-type line trend (Spearman line vs over-split flag): exact_repeat rho=-0.062 p=0.70 (FLAT); addition rho=-0.154 p=0.11; de_escalation rho=+0.556 p=0.0004 (RISING/inverted). De-escalation over-split rate by line: L2 0/15=0%, L3 8/12=67%, L4 2/4=50% (de_esc L2 vs L>=3: 0/15 vs 14/22, Fisher p=0.0001). Exact-repeat over-split rate stays high and flat: L2 9/13=69%, L3 5/6=83%, L4 5/7=71%, L5 3/4=75%, L6 2/2=100%. Logistic over-split~line+type (ref=other): line beta=-0.019 (OR=0.98, near-null after type control), exact_repeat OR=109, de_escalation OR=26, addition OR=8. KS/MW on raw line number across types are all null (Kruskal H=0.02 p=0.99; all pairwise KS p>0.2) because line-number alone is uninformative once type is known.
finding.effect_size: Type dominates line: conditional over-split odds ratios vs "other" are 109x (exact_repeat), 26x (de_escalation), 8x (addition), while line itself has OR=0.98 (null) after controlling for type. De-escalation L2-vs-L3+ risk difference = 0% vs 64% (rate ratio undefined/infinite; Fisher p=0.0001). Exact-repeat within-type line slope rho=-0.06 (flat) vs de-escalation rho=+0.56 (rising) — opposite-signed sub-curves.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 vs ALIGN n=706 (TRANS n=780). Sub-type n: exact_repeat=30, addition=17, de_escalation=14, other=13. Type denominators among all 780 transitions: exact_repeat 42, addition 111, de_escalation 37, other 590. Key anomaly cell: de-escalation at line 2 = 0/15 over-splits.
finding.caveats: Small per-type cells (de_escalation n=14 over-splits across only 37 transitions; L4+ buckets have single-digit denominators), so the de-escalation rising trend rests on the L2=0/15 vs L3=8/12 contrast — robust by Fisher (p=0.0001) but driven by few patients. Type classification uses set relations on parsed_drugs_repaired; "exact_repeat" (identical drug set to prior row) likely captures bracket-phase/maintenance continuations the doctor counts as the same line, and mis-parsing could shuffle a few rows between exact_repeat and de_escalation. Line number = cota_lot_numeric (COTA's own count, which is inflated for over-splits); using doctor line could shift exact assignments. The de-escalation inversion may partly reflect that early de-escalations (induction->maintenance at L1->L2) are correctly handled while later de-escalations confuse COTA — a clinical alternative I cannot fully separate from sample noise. Not corrected for patient-level clustering (some patients contribute multiple over-splits).
finding.method: Canonical load of sheet All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid then _original_row_order. Parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into a lowercased frozenset per row; computed prior-row set via groupby(cpid).shift(1). Classified each transition: cur==prev->exact_repeat, cur strict-subset prev->de_escalation, prev strict-subset cur->addition, else other. line=cota_lot_numeric. Over-split flag = transition_alignment_status=='candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split'. Computed (a) conditional over-split rate per type over all transitions of that type; (b) per-line over-split rate per type with transition-count denominators; (c) Spearman line-vs-over-split within each type; (d) Fisher exact on de_esc L2 vs L>=3; (e) chi2_contingency on type x over-split; (f) sklearn LogisticRegression (C=1e6) of over-split ~ line + type dummies (ref=other); (g) KS/MW/Kruskal on raw line distributions across types. Temp script: /tmp/lot6.py (and /tmp/lot3.py, /tmp/lot5.py).
finding.secondary_observations: (1) The headline decay-by-line is largely a COMPOSITION artifact: line-number has essentially no effect on over-split risk once transition type is controlled (logistic line OR=0.98). The published "peaks at line 2, decays to 0" curve is mostly the exact_repeat type (flat 71% risk) thinning out as identical-regimen continuations become rarer at high lines, not a genuine per-line error gradient. (2) Exact-regimen-repeat is the single highest-yield fix target: whenever the current drug set is identical to the immediately prior row, COTA wrongly starts a new line 71% of the time (30/42) regardless of line number — a deterministic-looking rule failure, likely bracket-phase/maintenance rows. (3) Additions are the most benign type (15% conditional risk) and mildly decay with line. (4) Raw line-number distributions are statistically indistinguishable across types (all KS p>0.2), which is itself the point: line tells you little; the drug-set transition type is what carries the signal.

verdict.recomputed: Independently re-parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into per-row frozensets, derived prior set via groupby(cpid).shift(1), and classified all 780 transitions. Every headline number reproduces exactly: type counts among 74 over-splits = exact_repeat 30, addition 17, de_escalation 14, other 13; conditional over-split rates = exact_repeat 30/42=71.4%, de_escalation 14/37=37.8%, addition 17/111=15.3%, other 13/590=2.2%; chi2_contingency=263.1, dof=3, p=9.45e-57; logistic over~line+type (C=1e6, ref=other): line beta=-0.019 OR=0.98, exact_repeat OR=109.4, de_escalation OR=26.0, addition OR=8.0; de-esc within-type Spearman vs COTA line rho=+0.556 p=0.0004; exact_repeat rho=-0.062 p=0.696; de-esc COTA-line L2 0/15 vs L>=3 14/22 Fisher p=0.0001. ATTACK using doctor (ground-truth) line instead of COTA's inflated line: de-esc Spearman rho collapses to +0.012 p=0.942; de-esc doctor-line L2 9/24=37.5% vs L>=3 5/13=38.5% Fisher p=1.00 (flat, NOT inverted). De-esc over rows have COTA mean line=4.0 but doctor mean=2.7 (gap +1 in 10, +2 in 4), confirming over-splits are mechanically pushed to higher COTA-line buckets. All 14 de-esc over-splits come from 14 distinct patients (no within-patient clustering).
verdict.corrected_effect: The type>line conclusion holds (chi2=263, ORs 109/26/8 vs line OR=0.98) and exact_repeat is genuinely flat and high-yield (71%, 30/42) — that part matches. But the novel headline (de-escalation as an INVERTED sub-curve, 0 at line 2 rising thereafter, opposite the early peak) does NOT hold: it is an artifact of plotting against COTA's own inflated line number. Using doctor ground-truth line, de-escalation over-split risk is FLAT (~38% at every line, rho=+0.01 p=0.94, L2-vs-L3+ Fisher p=1.0). Corrected framing: type carries the signal, line does not; the de-esc 'inversion' and 'opposite-signed sub-curves' claim should be dropped.
verdict.main_confound: Line axis = cota_lot_numeric, which is inflated precisely by the over-split being measured. De-escalation over-splits raise COTA's line by +1/+2, mechanically shifting them out of COTA-line-2 into line 3+ and manufacturing a spurious 'rising' (inverted) trend. Swapping to the doctor's ground-truth line eliminates the entire effect (rho +0.556->+0.012; Fisher p 0.0001->1.00).
verdict.critique: The colleague's caveats actually named this confound ('Line number = cota_lot_numeric ... using doctor line could shift exact assignments') but then proceeded to build the novel claim on the COTA-line trend anyway and rated it medium confidence. The single most load-bearing cell, de-esc L2=0/15, is the direct fingerprint of the artifact: an over-split cannot remain at COTA line 2, so de-esc over-splits are definitionally excluded from the L2 bucket. The robust, reproducible parts (type dominates line; exact_repeat flat and high-yield) are worth keeping, but the de-escalation 'inverted curve' is the kind of small-n, wrong-denominator pattern the rigor rules warn against. n=14 de-esc over-splits across 6 line buckets is also far too thin to assert any within-type trend regardless of axis.

raw_findings.title: The 'swing drug': which specific drugs trigger over-splits

finding.claim: The swing drug that disproportionately triggers COTA over-splits is not any of the hypothesized backbone agents (dexamethasone/lenalidomide/daratumumab/bortezomib) — those are actually DEPLETED in over-splits — but rather the addition of the transplant-conditioning step (melphalan + autologous SCT added together), which COTA treats as a new line while the doctor does not.
finding.evidence: Swing = a drug added or removed vs the patient's previous row. Among 74 OVER vs 706 ALIGN transitions: the four hypothesized candidates are NOT enriched and mostly significantly DEPLETED as swing drugs — daratumumab OVER 2/74 (2.7%) vs ALIGN 289/706 (40.9%), RR=0.07, p<1e-4; bortezomib 13/74 (17.6%) vs 222/706 (31.4%), RR=0.56, p=0.016; lenalidomide 18/74 (24.3%) vs 225/706 (31.9%), RR=0.76, p=0.24 (ns); dexamethasone 14/74 (18.9%) vs 156/706 (22.1%), RR=0.86, p=0.66 (ns); pomalidomide RR=0.33, carfilzomib 0/74 (p<1e-4). The only generalizable ENRICHED swing is transplant: autologous SCT ADDED 9/74 (12.2%, 8 distinct patients) vs 33/706 (4.7%), RR=2.60, OR=2.82, Fisher p=0.013; melphalan ADDED 9/74 vs 39/706, RR=2.20, p=0.037 — and all 9 melphalan-added OVER rows are also SCT-added (perfect co-occurrence = the conditioning signature). Combined "transplant added" 9/74 (12.2%) vs 41/706 (5.8%), RR=2.09, OR=2.25, p=0.044. NOTE: clarithromycin showed the largest raw rate ratio (RR=29, p=0.003, OVER 3/74 vs ALIGN 1/706) but all 3 events are from a SINGLE patient (cpid b739c87a) cycling clarithromycin on/off — a single-patient artifact, not a real swing drug.
finding.effect_size: Transplant-conditioning ADDED as swing: rate ratio 2.09 (12.2% vs 5.8%), OR 2.25, risk difference +6.4pp; line-number-adjusted logistic OR 1.80. In the opposite direction, classic backbone drugs are protective swings (daratumumab RR 0.07, carfilzomib RR 0, bortezomib RR 0.56).
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 transitions vs ALIGN n=706 transitions (780 total, baseline 136 excluded). Transplant-added over-splits: 9 rows across 8 distinct patients. Clarithromycin artifact: 3 rows, 1 patient.
finding.caveats: n=74 over-splits is small; the transplant-addition Fisher p (0.044) is borderline and would not survive multiple-testing correction across ~35 drugs tested. Line number is a partial confound: transplant occurs early (lines 2-4) exactly where over-split rate already peaks; within the early stratum (cota_lot<=4) the contrast weakens to 20.5% vs 11.2%, p=0.12 (ns), though it survives full-sample logistic adjustment (adj OR 1.80). 'autologous sct' and 'melphalan' are encoded as drug tokens in parsed_drugs_repaired, so this is COTA's representation of the conditioning step, not a separate procedure flag. The depletion of backbone drugs is partly mechanical (over-splits are dominated by same-regimen-repeats and drug-drops, so the big mono/doublet backbone drugs change less), so the 'protective' RRs reflect over-split composition rather than causal protection.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped cols, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. Parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into lowercased comma-split sets; built prev_dset = within-patient shift(1). For each transition row, swing set = (cur - prev) | (prev - cur); added = cur-prev; removed = prev-cur. For each drug with >=3 total events, built 2x2 (drug-swings yes/no) x (OVER/ALIGN) and ran scipy.stats.fisher_exact, computing OVER rate (/74), ALIGN rate (/706), rate ratio, OR, p. Repeated separately for ADDED-only and REMOVED-only. Checked patient spread per drug (n distinct cpid) to catch single-patient artifacts. Confound control: sklearn LogisticRegression of over ~ transplant_add + cota_lot_numeric, plus stratified Fisher within cota_lot<=4.
finding.secondary_observations: Direction of swings in OVER: most-added = melphalan(9), autologous SCT(9), lenalidomide(7), pomalidomide(5); most-removed = lenalidomide(11), bortezomib(10), dexamethasone(10), autologous SCT(5). The transplant signal is overwhelmingly an ADDITION event (9 added vs 5 removed). The hypothesis-as-stated is essentially a null result for the four named candidate drugs — none are enriched, refuting the prior assumption that common backbone agents drive over-splits; instead over-splits are enriched for transplant-step additions and (compositionally) for same-set/drug-drop transitions where backbone drugs do not change.

verdict.recomputed: Reproduced the full pipeline from the canonical frame (74 OVER / 706 ALIGN / 136 baseline). Swing-drug 2x2 Fisher tests match the claim row-for-row: daratumumab OVER 2/74 vs ALIGN 289/706, RR 0.066, p=1.8e-13; bortezomib 13/74 vs 222/706, RR 0.56, p=0.016; lenalidomide 18/74 vs 225/706, RR 0.76, p=0.23 (ns); dexamethasone 14/74 vs 156/706, RR 0.86, p=0.66 (ns); pomalidomide RR 0.33, p=3.3e-5; carfilzomib 0/74 vs 235/706, p=1e-12. Transplant ADDED (melphalan|autologous sct) 9/74 (8 distinct patients) vs 41/706, RR 2.09, OR 2.25, Fisher p=0.044; melphalan-added and sct-added co-occur perfectly (9/9). Clarithromycin is a confirmed single-patient artifact (cpid b739c87a, 3 swing events all one patient). Line-adjusted logistic adj OR for transplant-add = 1.80; early-line (cota_lot<=4) stratified Fisher p=0.12. Leave-one-patient-out: dropping any of the 8 transplant patients raises p to 0.12-0.20. Bonferroni over 35 tested drugs -> corrected p ~1.5.
verdict.corrected_effect: Backbone-depletion half is real and strong (daratumumab/carfilzomib/pomalidomide depleted at p<1e-4; effect sizes reproduce exactly) — this part holds. Transplant-enrichment half (RR 2.09, p=0.044) is real in the full sample but too fragile to headline: fails leave-one-patient-out (any of 8 patients dropped -> p 0.12-0.20), fails Bonferroni (35 drugs -> corrected p ~1.5), and is line-confounded (early-line stratum p=0.12). Corrected framing: 'transplant addition is a suggestive, line-confounded, multiplicity-fragile enrichment (9 events, 8 patients), not an established swing driver.' Minor: claim's early-stratum figures (20.5% vs 11.2%) did not reproduce; I get 16.7% vs 8.9% — same conclusion, different denominators.
verdict.main_confound: Line number plus multiplicity/single-patient fragility: transplant occurs at lines 2-4 where over-split rate already peaks, the 9-event signal rests on 8 patients so no single patient can be removed without losing significance, and it does not survive Bonferroni across 35 drugs tested.
verdict.critique: Arithmetic and denominators are correct and the ALIGN control is the right comparator — I could not fault the computation. The depletion finding is robust and genuinely refutes the naive 'common backbone drug drives over-splits' prior, a valuable null. But the novel positive claim (transplant = the swing) rests on n=9 over a borderline p=0.044 that evaporates under every standard robustness check (LOPO, Bonferroni, line stratification). The claim transparently lists these weaknesses in its caveats, yet still elevates transplant to 'the swing drug' in the headline. Per the rigor rules (humility at n=74, control the obvious confound, default toward weakened), the positive half is suggestive at best. Verdict weakened: depletion confirmed, transplant enrichment real-but-fragile-and-confounded.

finding.claim: The induction-to-maintenance "collapse to a single maintenance agent" motif is NOT a driver of COTA over-splits; multi-drug -> single-agent transitions are actually depleted among over-splits, while over-splits are enriched for transitions that stay multi-drug (current >=3 drugs).
finding.evidence: Drug counts from parsed_drugs_repaired (identical with parsed_drugs). multi->single (prev>=2 drugs -> cur==1 drug): OVER 2/74 = 2.7% vs ALIGN 70/706 = 9.9%; Fisher OR=0.25, RR=0.27, p=0.054. Reverse single->multi: OVER 4/74 = 5.4% vs ALIGN 49/706 = 6.9% (not enriched). Of the 2 OVER multi->single cases, agents were lenalidomide(1) and daratumumab(1) — too few to claim lenalidomide dominance; in ALIGN the dominant maintenance single-agents were daratumumab(22), investigational(11), bendamustine(6), belantamab(6), lenalidomide(5). Mann-Whitney on current drug-count: OVER mean cur_n=2.78 vs ALIGN 2.60, p=0.009. The actual enrichment is the opposite motif: cur_n>=3 drugs in OVER 50/74=67.6% vs ALIGN 354/706=50.1%, Fisher OR=2.07, p=0.0048.
finding.effect_size: multi->single is ~3.7x LESS common in over-splits (OR=0.25, RR=0.27); adjusted for line number OR=0.41. Conversely staying multi-drug (cur>=3) is ~2x MORE common (OR=2.07, p=0.0048).
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 (all have a valid previous row) vs ALIGN n=706; multi->single subgroup OVER n=2, ALIGN n=70.
finding.caveats: The multi->single Fisher is borderline (p=0.054) and the OVER cell is tiny (n=2), so the "depletion" is suggestive not definitive; with only 2 events the lenalidomide-vs-other agent question is unanswerable. multi->single concentrates at later lines (ALIGN cases peak at lines 5-10) where over-split rate is intrinsically low, which is a partial line-number confound — but a logistic regression adjusting for line still gives ms OR=0.41 (protective direction preserved), and the line 2-10 stratum keeps OR=0.27. The cur_n>=3 enrichment could itself be partly a line-number artifact (early lines have more drugs and more over-splits); I did not fully stratify that secondary result.
finding.method: Canonical load of All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. Parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into a lowercased drug set per row (split on , and ; stripping brackets/quotes); prev_set = within-patient shift(1); cur_n/prev_n = set sizes. Restricted to transition rows with a valid prev_n. Defined multi->single = (prev_n>=2 & cur_n==1) and single->multi = (prev_n==1 & cur_n>=2). Compared rates OVER vs ALIGN with scipy.stats.fisher_exact; rate ratios computed directly. Mann-Whitney (mannwhitneyu) on cur_n. Confound control via sklearn LogisticRegression of over ~ [ms, cota_lot_numeric] and Fisher within line strata 2-4 and 2-10. Tallied single-agent identity with Counter over cur_set for multi->single rows.
finding.secondary_observations: The dominant maintenance single-agent in this cohort overall is daratumumab, not lenalidomide (ALIGN multi->single: dara 22 vs lena 5), contradicting the "classically single-agent lenalidomide" assumption embedded in the hypothesis. The real over-split signal points toward multi-drug regimen RESHUFFLES (cur_n>=3, drug-set changes that keep drug count high) rather than de-intensification to maintenance — consistent with the known subset patterns (same-set-different-structure, drug additions) being where COTA over-counts.

verdict.recomputed: Independently reran the full pipeline. Reproduced every headline number exactly. multi->single (prev>=2 & cur==1): OVER 2/74=2.7% vs ALIGN 70/706=9.9%, Fisher OR=0.252, RR=0.273, p=0.0537. single->multi: OVER 4/74=5.4% vs ALIGN 49/706=6.9%, OR=0.766, p=0.81 (not enriched). cur_n>=3: OVER 50/74=67.6% vs ALIGN 354/706=50.1%, OR=2.072, p=0.0048. Mann-Whitney cur_n: OVER mean 2.78 vs ALIGN 2.60, p=0.0090. Confound controls reproduce: logistic over~ms+line OR_ms=0.412; over~cur3+line OR_cur3=1.955; stratum L2-10 ms OR=0.265 (p=0.051), cur3 OR=2.112 (p=0.0041). The 2 OVER multi->single agents are lenalidomide(1)+daratumumab(1); ALIGN dominant single-agent is daratumumab(22) not lenalidomide(5). Two additional checks I added that the colleague did NOT run, both strengthening the finding: (1) full line-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel ORs — cur3 CMH OR=2.019, ms CMH OR=0.32 — so BOTH effects survive complete line-number stratification, closing the caveat that cur_n>=3 might be a pure line artifact; (2) cur_n==1 regardless of prev: OVER 2/74 vs ALIGN 82/706, OR=0.211, p=0.016 — the depletion-of-collapse-to-single-agent is even stronger and robust to the prev>=2 conditioning.
verdict.corrected_effect: Matches. Minor correction to the stated method: parsed_drugs_repaired and parsed_drugs are NOT "identical" — they agree on only 88.4% of rows — but this is immaterial; both columns give the same multi->single, single->multi, cur3, and MW results (cur3 p shifts trivially 0.0048 vs 0.0031). The effect sizes (ms ~3.7x less common, OR 0.25; cur>=3 ~2x more common, OR 2.07) all hold.
verdict.main_confound: Line number was the obvious confound (multi->single concentrates at later low-over-split lines L5-10; early lines have both more drugs and more over-splits). I confirmed it is NOT driving either result: line-stratified CMH OR_ms=0.32 and OR_cur3=2.02, plus logistic adjustment (0.41 / 1.96) and within-stratum Fisher all preserve direction and near-significance. The only genuine weakness is statistical, not confounding: the multi->single OVER cell is n=2 (Fisher p=0.054, borderline), so "depletion" is suggestive at conventional thresholds. The colleague stated this honestly and the cur_n>=3 enrichment (p=0.0048) and cur_n==1 depletion (p=0.016) are independently significant, so the overall claim does not rest on the n=2 cell.
verdict.critique: The claim is conservative, the arithmetic is exact, the control (706 aligned transitions) is correct, and the caveats are unusually honest (flagging the n=2 cell and the borderline p). My only substantive nits: (1) the "identical columns" assertion is wrong (88.4% agreement) though harmless; (2) the colleague admitted not fully stratifying the cur_n>=3 result for line — I did (CMH OR=2.02) and it holds, so that caveat can be retired. The framing is sound: the induction->maintenance collapse motif is genuinely NOT where COTA over-splits; over-splits cluster at cur_n 2-3 (88%) and avoid single-agent endpoints. The "lenalidomide dominance" assumption in the original hypothesis is correctly debunked (dara dominates). This is a valid, well-defended null/reversal result.

raw_findings.title: Steroid/dexamethasone churn as a structural noise source

finding.claim: The assigned steroid-churn hypothesis is a NULL result: steroid-only changes explain only 2.7% of COTA over-splits and dexamethasone-drop shows no enrichment; the actual dominant noise source is that 40.5% of over-splits occur when the drug set is IDENTICAL to the prior row (mostly just a bracket-phase/maintenance-formatting change).
finding.evidence: Steroid hypothesis (NULL): steroid-only drug-set change = 2/74 OVER (2.7%) vs 1/706 ALIGN (0.1%); Fisher OR=19.6 p=0.025 but n is trivially small (only 2 of 74 over-splits), so it explains almost none of the over-split volume. Dexamethasone DROPPED: 10/74 OVER (13.5%) vs 90/706 ALIGN (12.7%), OR=1.07, RR=1.06, p=0.855 -> no enrichment. Dex ADDED: 4/74 (5.4%) vs 66/706 (9.3%), OR=0.55, p=0.39. ANY steroid changed: 18.9% OVER vs 23.4% ALIGN, OR=0.77, p=0.47 (if anything lower in over-splits). The real signal, found while testing: IDENTICAL drug set vs previous row = 30/74 OVER (40.5%) vs 12/706 ALIGN (1.7%), Fisher OR=39.4, RR=23.9, p=2.06e-24. Survives line-number control: logistic regression on all 780 transitions gives OR=25.2 for identical-set with line OR=0.92. Of the 30 identical-set over-splits, 21 have a changed bracket-phase count (a maintenance/phase formatting change) while the underlying drug set is unchanged; discontinue reasons: progression 11, toxicity 8, doctor_preference 6.
finding.effect_size: Steroid-only: 2.7% of over-splits (negligible share, hypothesis rejected as a driver). Dex-drop: RR=1.06 (no effect). Identical-drug-set (the real finding): risk difference 40.5% - 1.7% = +38.8 percentage points, rate ratio 23.9x, Fisher OR=39.4, adjusted (line-controlled) logistic OR=25.2.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 over-split rows vs ALIGN n=706 aligned transitions (780 transitions total). Steroid-only subgroup: 2 over-split rows. Identical-drug-set subgroup: 30 over-split / 12 aligned. Logistic fit on all 780 transitions.
finding.caveats: The steroid-only Fisher test reaches p=0.025 but rests on just 2 over-split events, so it is statistically fragile and clinically immaterial as a volume driver - the honest read is NULL for the steroid hypothesis, not a positive finding. The identical-drug-set finding is very strong (p=2e-24) but "identical drug set" partially overlaps the previously-known sub-label same_exact_regimen_repeated=20; this analysis extends it by (a) quantifying it against the ALIGN control with an effect size, (b) showing it survives line-number adjustment, and (c) showing 21/30 are driven purely by bracket-phase formatting differences rather than any drug change. Drug-set equality is computed from parsed_drugs_repaired with set-difference, so it ignores dose/schedule; a true clinical line change with identical drugs but different intent (e.g., re-induction) could be miscounted as "no change" - though the doctor-as-truth labeling already says these should NOT be new lines. Phase-count proxy uses bracket "[" counts.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped columns, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. Parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into lowercased drug-token sets (strip brackets/quotes, split on comma); built prev_dset = per-patient shift(1). For each transition (excluding baseline_first_lot_row), computed symmetric difference diff=(cur-prev)|(prev-cur). Classified: no_drug_change (diff empty), steroid_only_change (diff nonempty and every changed drug in {dexamethasone,prednisone,methylprednisolone,prednisolone}), else non_steroid_change. Compared OVER vs ALIGN shares with scipy.stats.fisher_exact and rate ratios. Separately flagged dex_dropped (dex in prev, not in cur), dex_added, any_steroid_changed and tested each with fisher_exact. For the identical-set finding, ran sklearn LogisticRegression of over-split indicator on [identical_set, cota_lot_numeric] across all 780 transitions to adjust for line number, and counted bracket "[" occurrences in line_of_therapy_name vs previous to test whether phase structure changed while drug set stayed identical.
finding.secondary_observations: Among the 30 identical-drug-set over-splits, 21 (70%) have a different number of bracket phases between the prior and current row - i.e., COTA opens a new line when a maintenance/continuation phase appears or drops off even though no drug is added or removed. This points to COTA's line logic being triggered by regimen-string phase formatting rather than by actual drug-therapy changes, which is a more actionable root cause than steroid churn. The identical-set over-splits span lines 2-9 and track the known decay curve (peak at line 2, 9/19), so this is not a single-line artifact.

verdict.recomputed: Re-parsed parsed_drugs_repaired into drug-token sets, built per-patient prev set, and recomputed all rates against the ALIGN control (74 over vs 706 aligned). Steroid-only change: 2/74 (2.7%) vs 1/706 (0.1%), Fisher OR=19.58, p=0.0250 — exact match. Dex dropped: 10/74 (13.5%) vs 90/706 (12.7%), OR=1.07, RR=1.06, p=0.855 — match. Dex added: 4/74 vs 66/706, OR=0.55, p=0.39 — match. Any steroid changed: 14/74 (18.9%) vs 165/706 (23.4%), OR=0.77, p=0.468 — match (if anything lower in over-splits). Identical drug set: 30/74 (40.5%) vs 12/706 (1.7%), Fisher OR=39.43, RR=23.85, p=2.06e-24 — exact match. Line-adjusted sklearn logistic: OR_identical=25.2 with C=1.0 (default reg), 38.8 unregularized; line OR=0.92 both ways. Bracket-phase: 21/30 identical-set over-splits changed phase count; lines 2-9 (9 at line 2); discontinue progression 11/toxicity 8/doctor_preference 6 — all exact.
verdict.corrected_effect: matches (one minor note: the "adjusted logistic OR=25.2" is the C=1.0 regularized sklearn estimate; the unregularized adjusted OR is ~38.8. Both are large and both show line-number OR~0.92, so line is not the confound either way. Substance unchanged.)
verdict.main_confound: None that breaks the finding. The obvious confound (line number) was correctly controlled: in the adjusted logistic, line OR=0.92 (slightly protective) while identical-set OR stays 25-39, and the identical-set over-splits span lines 2-9 tracking the known decay curve, so it is not a single-line artifact. The honest residual caveat is conceptual overlap: "identical drug set" largely subsumes the previously-known same_exact_regimen_repeated=20 sub-label, so the genuinely novel contribution is the ALIGN-control effect size, the line-adjustment, and the bracket-phase mechanism (21/30) — not the existence of repeated regimens per se.
verdict.critique: Arithmetic and denominators are correct and the steroid NULL is honestly reported (the p=0.025 steroid-only result is appropriately disclaimed as resting on 2 events and immaterial as a volume driver, not spun as positive). The pivot to identical-drug-set is statistically overwhelming (p=2e-24) and robust to the line confound. Two soft critiques, neither fatal: (1) the reported adjusted OR=25.2 silently depends on sklearn's default L2 penalty — defensible for n=74 but should be labeled as regularized; (2) novelty is partial since identical-set overlaps the known same_exact_regimen_repeated label, and the bracket-"[" phase-count proxy is crude (counts brackets, not validated phase semantics). The set-difference also ignores dose/schedule, but doctor-as-truth labeling already deems these non-lines, so that cuts in the finding's favor.

raw_findings.title: Line duration & inter-line time gaps vs over-split (unused date columns)

finding.claim: COTA over-splits are not short fragments and do not have generally smaller inter-line gaps; the only date-based signal is a modest excess of near-zero/zero gaps (current line starts the same day or 1 day after the previous line ended), consistent with COTA chopping a seamless continuation into two lines.
finding.evidence: Date columns parsed for all rows; durations/gaps computed per patient (sorted by cpid,_original_row_order). CURRENT line duration: OVER median 136d (n=73) vs ALIGN 129d (n=671), MWU p=0.43, rank-biserial -0.06 (NULL). PREVIOUS line duration: OVER median 114d vs ALIGN 159d, MWU p=0.23 (NULL). GAP (cur_start - prev_end): OVER median 17d vs ALIGN 21d, MWU p=0.51 (NULL on central tendency). The signal is only in the near-zero tail: gap==0 OVER 10/73=13.7% vs ALIGN 58/699=8.3% (OR 1.75, Fisher p=0.13); gap<=1d OVER 19/73=26.0% vs ALIGN 114/699=16.3% (OR 1.81, RR 1.55, Fisher p=0.049). Effect peaks exactly at gap<=1 and decays both directions (gap<0 p=0.44; gap<=0 p=0.084; gap<=1 p=0.049; gap<=2 p=0.082; gap<=3 p=0.16; gap<=7 p=0.22), the shape of a real near-zero-gap excess rather than a global shift. Overlapping (negative) gaps are NOT enriched (OVER 8.2% vs ALIGN 5.9%, p=0.44).
finding.effect_size: gap<=1 day: odds ratio 1.81, risk ratio 1.55, absolute risk difference +9.7 percentage points (26.0% vs 16.3%). Duration effects negligible (rank-biserial |r|<0.09).
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 (73 with computable gap/duration; 1 dropped as patient-first row) vs ALIGN n=706 (699 with gap, 671 with duration). gap<=1 OVER rows come from 16 distinct patients (14 contribute 1 row each), so not a single-patient artifact.
finding.caveats: The single significant result (gap<=1, p=0.049) is borderline and not multiple-comparison corrected across the ~6 thresholds and 3 metrics tested; under any correction it is non-significant. n=74 gives wide CIs. The duration and gap-central-tendency hypotheses are firmly NULL, so the original "over-splits are short fragments / overlapping continuations" hypothesis is mostly NOT supported. Line-number is a partial confound (over-splits peak at line 2-4) but adjusting for cota_lot_numeric in logistic regression barely moves the gap<=1 OR (1.73 univariate -> 1.73 adjusted; lot OR 0.91), so line number does not explain it. Only 8/19 near-zero-gap over-splits also have the same drug-family as the prior line, so the "seamless continuation" mechanism is suggestive, not confirmed.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped columns, sorted by cpid then _original_row_order. Parsed date_start/date_end_line_of_therapy to datetime. dur=end-start (days); within groupby(cpid), prev_end=shift(end), gap=start-prev_end, prev_dur=shift(dur). Split by transition_alignment_status into OVER (candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split) and ALIGN (transition_aligned). Continuous comparisons: scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu two-sided + medians/IQR + rank-biserial. Threshold comparisons: scipy.stats.fisher_exact 2x2 on gap<=thr for thr in {0,1,2,3,7,14} plus gap<0. Confound control: sklearn LogisticRegression of over ~ gap_le1 + cota_lot_numeric, plus per-line stratified rates. Verified patient clustering via cpid.nunique on the gap<=1 over rows.
finding.secondary_observations: Median gap is slightly SMALLER for over-splits (17d vs 21d) and previous-line duration slightly shorter (114d vs 159d), both directionally consistent with the continuation hypothesis but non-significant. The gap<=1 enrichment is concentrated in lines 3-4 (lot=3: OVER gap<=1 rate 0.41 vs ALIGN 0.15; lot=4: 0.33 vs 0.17), while line 2 shows no difference (0.17 vs 0.16) - the date artifact may matter more for mid-line splits than for the early-line peak. ALIGN gaps have a much longer right tail (max 3992d vs OVER max 755d), reflecting genuinely separate later lines in the control group.

verdict.recomputed: Reloaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order, parsed dates, computed dur=end-start, within-patient gap=start-prev_end, prev_dur=shift. Every number reproduces. CUR dur: OVER median 136 (n=73) vs ALIGN 129 (n=671), MWU p=0.432. PREV dur: OVER 114 vs ALIGN 159, p=0.227. GAP central: OVER median 17 (n=73) vs ALIGN 21 (n=699), p=0.513 -- all NULL as claimed. Thresholds (Fisher 2x2): gap<0 OR1.44 p=0.437; gap<=0 OR1.70 p=0.084; gap==0 OR1.75 p=0.129; gap<=1 OR1.81 RR1.60 p=0.0491; gap<=2 p=0.082; gap<=3 p=0.159; gap<=7 p=0.216. Decay-around-gap<=1 shape confirmed. gap<=1 over rows = 19 from 16 distinct patients (14 contribute 1 each). Logistic over~gap_le1: OR 1.73 univariate, 1.73 adjusted for cota_lot (lot OR 0.91) -- line number does NOT explain it. Stratified: lot=2 0.17 vs 0.16 (no diff), lot=3 0.41 vs 0.15, lot=4 0.33 vs 0.17. Multiple-comparison check: min p=0.049, Bonferroni x11 = 0.54, BH min = 0.29 -- nothing survives correction, exactly as the caveat states.
verdict.corrected_effect: matches. Duration effects negligible (|rank-biserial|<0.09); central gap NULL; only signal is gap<=1 near-zero tail excess OR~1.8, RR~1.6, +9.7pp (26.0% vs 16.3%), p=0.049 uncorrected and non-significant after correction. Framing as a low-confidence, mostly-null result with a suggestive near-zero tail is accurate.
verdict.main_confound: Line number was the obvious confound and was correctly ruled out (logistic-adjusted OR unchanged at 1.73). The residual weakness is statistical, not a confound: the single significant test (gap<=1, p=0.049) does not survive multiple-comparison correction, and the "peak exactly at gap<=1" is likely noise within a small near-zero region. The colleague flags all of this explicitly.
verdict.critique: The headline claim is a NULL (durations and central gaps no different from controls), which is rock-solid and reproduces exactly. The one positive signal is appropriately downgraded to low confidence and the author honestly states it fails any correction. Minor over-reach: presenting "peaks exactly at gap<=1, decays both directions" as evidence of a real excess slightly oversells noise, since gap<=0/<=1/<=2 p-values (0.084/0.049/0.082) are statistically indistinguishable -- the exact peak location is not meaningful. But this is self-disclosed in the caveats and does not change the verdict. A correctly-reported near-null with proper control adjustment and honest correction discussion is exactly what should be confirmed.

raw_findings.title: discontinue_reason: does COTA over-split at non-progression / undocumented points?

finding.claim: COTA over-splits occur disproportionately at transitions where the prior line ended with NO documented discontinuation reason (blank): the line-defining clinical event is undocumented, and the correct row to attribute that event to is the PREVIOUS row, not the current row.
finding.evidence: Attributing each transition's line-ending event to the PREVIOUS row's discontinue_reason (semantically: why the line that just ended ended), 32.4% of over-splits (24/74) follow a prior line with a BLANK reason vs 12.9% of aligned transitions (91/706): Fisher OR=3.24, p<0.0001, bootstrap 95% CI [1.82, 5.48]. Collapsing to progression-vs-not: over-splits lack a documented progression in 67.6% (50/74) vs 46.9% (331/706) of aligned (OR=2.36, p=0.0009). The 'other documented' bucket (toxicity/doctor_preference, no progression) is flat (35.1% OVER vs 34.0% ALIGN), so the signal is specifically the UNDOCUMENTED (blank) category, not toxicity/preference. Crucially the attribution matters: using the CURRENT row's reason gives a null result (no-progression 44.6% OVER vs 52.5% ALIGN, OR=0.73, p=0.22) — the verified-facts base rates used the wrong (current) row.
finding.effect_size: Blank prior-line reason: OR=3.24 (95% CI 1.82-5.48), risk difference +19.5pp (32.4% vs 12.9%), rate ratio 2.51. Progression-absent: OR=2.36, risk diff +20.7pp.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 vs ALIGN n=706 (780 transitions). Blank-prev cells: OVER 24, ALIGN 91. Line-stratified subsets: lines 2-4 OVER n=48, lines 2-10 OVER n=71.
finding.caveats: n=74 over-splits is small; the 24 blank-prev over-splits is a modest cell though the OR CI excludes 1 comfortably. discontinue_reason has missingness that is itself the exposure, so 'blank' may partly reflect general documentation sparsity at certain transitions rather than a true absence of a clinical event; I cannot distinguish 'no event occurred' from 'event occurred but not coded.' Multi-reason backslash-joined strings were treated by substring-matching 'progression' anywhere; results are stable under a first-token rule. The previous-row attribution is my reasoned semantic choice (validated against a worked patient example where row N's reason describes why line N ends), but the data dictionary does not state it explicitly.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped cols, sorted by cpid,_original_row_order. Built prev_discontinue_reason = groupby(cpid).discontinue_reason.shift(1). Defined OVER=candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split (74), ALIGN=transition_aligned (706). Classified each transition's prev reason as blank (NaN) / progression (substring 'progression' anywhere) / other_documented. Ran scipy.stats.fisher_exact on 2x2 [OVER,ALIGN] x [blank, not-blank] and x [no-progression, progression] for BOTH current-row and prev-row attributions. Controlled for line number via (a) sklearn LogisticRegression is_over ~ prev_blank + line (prev_blank OR=3.23, line OR=0.91; prev_blank and line uncorrelated, mean line 5.12 vs 5.13) and (b) Fisher within line strata 2-4 (OR=3.21,p=0.0012) and 2-10 (OR=3.13,p=0.0001). 5000-rep bootstrap for OR CI. Orthogonality to known drug-drop pattern checked via parsed_drugs subset test (current set subset-or-equal of previous).
finding.secondary_observations: The blank-prev signal is largely ORTHOGONAL to the known de-escalation/drug-drop subset pattern: only 25% (6/24) of blank-prev over-splits are de-escalation/same-set, versus 72% (36/50) of documented-prev over-splits — so the known subset sub-patterns cluster among DOCUMENTED transitions while undocumented-event over-splits are a distinct failure mode. Also methodologically important: the row-attribution choice flips the result entirely (current-row reason p=0.22 null vs prev-row p=0.0009), suggesting the team's existing 'blank ~24% OVER vs ~16% ALIGN' base rate was computed on the current row and understated the true effect; on the prev row it is 32.4% vs 12.9%.

verdict.recomputed: Independently reloaded All_COTA_With_Transitions (74 OVER, 706 ALIGN, 136 baseline confirmed). Built prev_discontinue_reason via groupby(cpid).shift(1). PREV-ROW blank: 24/74 (32.4%) OVER vs 91/706 (12.9%) ALIGN, Fisher OR=3.244, p=4.24e-5 — exact match to claim. Bootstrap 5000-rep OR 95% CI [1.84, 5.49] (claim [1.82,5.48]). Progression-absent (prev): 50/74 (67.6%) vs 331/706 (46.9%), OR=2.36, p=0.00087. CURRENT-row no-progression: 44.6% vs 52.5%, OR=0.727, p=0.222 (null) — the attribution flip is real and reproduces. 'Other documented' bucket flat: 35.1% vs 34.0%. Confounds: logistic is_over~prev_blank+line gives prev_blank OR=2.98, line OR=0.91; prev_blank uncorrelated with line (mean line 5.13 vs 5.12). Survives line strata: lines2-4 OR=3.21 p=0.0012, lines2-10 OR=3.13 p=0.00012, lines>=3 excluding L2 OR=2.75 p=0.0043 (25.5% vs 11.0%). Direction holds at EVERY line (L2 53%v22%, L3 18%v11%, L4 25%v7%, etc). Transplant blank-rate flat (14% vs 16%). 24 events span 21 patients (not clustered). First-token progression rule even stronger (78.4% vs 58.5%, p=0.0007). Orthogonality: de-escalation 25% among blank-prev vs 64% among documented-prev.
verdict.corrected_effect: matches — OR=3.24 (95% CI 1.84-5.49), risk diff +19.5pp (32.4% vs 12.9%), rate ratio 2.51. All effect-size figures reproduce. Minor note: the claim's secondary-obs '72% de-escalation among documented-prev' came out as 64% under my parsed_drugs subset definition, but the direction and conclusion (subset patterns cluster among documented transitions, blank-prev is a distinct mode) are identical. Also the claim's 'mean line 5.12 vs 5.13' refers to line conditional on prev_blank (which I confirm); the unconditional mean line differs (OVER 4.49 vs ALIGN 5.18), but that does not threaten the finding since prev_blank itself is line-independent and the effect survives stratification.
verdict.main_confound: Informative missingness: 'blank' discontinue_reason is the exposure but may reflect general documentation sparsity rather than a true absence of a clinical event — the data cannot distinguish 'no event occurred' from 'event occurred but uncoded.' This is acknowledged in the caveats and is inherent to the question, not a fixable flaw. The obvious mechanical confounds (line number, transplant, patient clustering, multi-reason parsing) were all tested and ruled out.
verdict.critique: The finding is arithmetically correct, the control group is right, and the effect is robust to every confound I attacked: line number (stratified + logistic + survives L2 removal), transplant, patient clustering (21 patients), and parsing rule. The previous-row vs current-row attribution flip is the genuinely novel contribution and it reproduces cleanly (p=0.0009 vs p=0.22). Remaining honest weaknesses, all already disclosed: (1) the 24-event cell is small so the point OR is imprecise though the CI excludes 1 with room; (2) the prev-row attribution is a defensible semantic choice not stated in the dictionary — but the worked logic (row N's reason = why line N ended) is sound and the result holds; (3) informative missingness means the causal interpretation ('undocumented clinical event') is one reading of a correlation between blankness and over-splitting. None of these undermine the statistical claim. Confidence label 'high' is justified.

raw_findings.title: What drives big over-splits (+2..+5) vs single (+1)?

finding.claim: Severe over-counting is NOT caused by any single transition jumping more than +1 — every one of the 74 over-splits is a per-transition jump of exactly +1, so large cumulative shifts (+2..+5) are purely "repeat offender" patients accumulating multiple separate +1 over-splits; these repeat offenders are heavily-pretreated patients, and high total-line count independently raises the per-transition over-split rate even beyond the known line-number decay.
finding.evidence: Per-transition jump (cota_inc - doc_inc) = +1 for ALL 74/74 over-splits; cota_inc=+1 (74/74), doc_inc=0 (74/74). Zero single-transition jumps >1 exist. Cumulative shift counts: +1=52, +2=17, +3=3, +4=1, +5=1 rows. Per patient, max cumulative shift EXACTLY equals number of over-split rows for all 52 offenders (no mismatches): 35 patients have 1 over-split, 14 have 2, 2 have 3, 1 has 5. The single +4 and +5 rows both belong to ONE patient (b739c87a) who over-split 5 separate times (cum shifts 1,2,3,4,5). Repeat offenders (>=2 over-splits, n=17 patients) have far more total COTA lines than single offenders (n=35): mean 10.41 vs 7.17, median 11 vs 7 (Mann-Whitney p=0.0004). Per-transition over-split rate: repeat pooled 24.4% (39/160) vs single 16.2% (35/216), MWU p=0.0042. Transition-level logistic P(over-split) ~ line + patient_total_lines: line coef=-0.215 (known decay), total_lines coef=+0.182 POSITIVE; LR test adding total_lines to line-only model chi2=20.98, p<0.0001. Stratified de-confound: among EARLY transitions (line<=4), patients with >=8 total lines over-split at 16.7% (23/138) vs 9.7% (25/259) for <8 lines, Fisher OR=1.87, p=0.052. Big-shift rows (>=2) occur mechanically LATER (mean line 6.95 vs 3.44, MWU p<0.0001). Big-shift rows show NO transplant/CAR-T/bispecific enrichment (9.1% vs 13.5%, Fisher OR=0.64, p=0.72), NO drug-count difference (2.77 vs 2.69, p=0.83), and similar discontinue-reason/subset-direction mix.
finding.effect_size: Direction: all over-splits are atomic +1 events (100%, 74/74) — large shifts are accumulation, never a single big jump. Repeat-vs-single total lines: median 11 vs 7. Independent total-lines effect: logistic coef +0.182 per line (LR chi2=21, p<0.0001). De-confounded rate ratio among early lines: 16.7%/9.7% = 1.73x (OR 1.87). Null effects for big vs +1 rows: transplant OR=0.64 (p=0.72), drug count diff ~0.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 rows across 52 patients (35 single, 17 repeat) vs ALIGN n=706 / 780 total transitions; 136 patients total. Big-shift rows n=22 (>=2) vs +1 rows n=52. Early-line stratum (line<=4): n=397 transitions (138 in >=8-line patients, 259 in <8).
finding.caveats: The atomic-+1 result is definitional/exact (no statistics needed). The "high-line-burden raises rate" claim is the weaker, contestable part: the de-confounded early-line test is borderline (p=0.052, only 23 events in the high-burden cell) and could reflect residual confounding (heavily pretreated patients have more drug switching/de-escalation events that COTA mis-splits, i.e. total-lines may be a proxy for disease complexity rather than a driver). The Poisson clustering test (observed 17 repeat offenders vs null-expected ~15, p=0.35) shows the NUMBER of repeat offenders is consistent with pure opportunity, so the elevated rate is modest, not a strong distinct clustering. n=74 overall; subgroup tests are underpowered and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Transplant/CAR-T flag is a regex over regimen text and may misclassify.
finding.method: Canonical load of All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. (1) Computed cota_inc=cota_lot-previous_cota_lot, doc_inc=doctor_lot-previous_doctor_lot, per_trans_jump=cota_inc-doc_inc on the 74 OVER rows; value_counts. (2) Grouped OVER by cpid to count over-split rows/patient; compared to per-patient max cumulative shift; verified equality and listed each multi-row patient's shift sequence. (3) Defined repeat (>=2 over-splits) vs single (==1) patients; compared total COTA lines (max cota_lot_numeric per patient) and total rows via Mann-Whitney (alternative=greater). (4) Per-transition over-split rate per offender patient = n_over/n_transitions; MWU repeat vs single. (5) Poisson opportunity simulation (20000 draws, rate=74/780 x n_trans per patient) for P(>=2). (6) sklearn LogisticRegression on transitions: over ~ line; over ~ line+totlines; manual deviance LR chi2 test (C=1e6). (7) Stratified Fisher exact on early transitions (line<=4) by patient totlines>=8. (8) For big(>=2) vs +1 rows: MWU on line number and drug count (parsed_drugs comma-split), Fisher on transplant/CAR-T regex flag, crosstabs of first discontinue_reason (split on backslash) and prev-vs-current drug-set subset direction.
finding.secondary_observations: The known line-number decay is reconfirmed (logistic line coef -0.215). The single 5x-over-split patient (b739c87a) is the sole source of every +3/+4/+5 cumulative row and is an extreme outlier worth manual chart review. Discontinue-reason mix is dominated by progression in both groups (big 11/22, +1 20/52) and does not distinguish severity. Subset direction (same/de-escalation/addition) is similar across big vs +1, so severity is not driven by a particular transition type — it is driven by treatment exposure (number of opportunities) plus a mild rate elevation in high-burden patients.

verdict.corrected_effect: Part 1 (all over-splits are atomic +1; big cumulative shifts are accumulation of multiple +1 events) fully confirmed 74/74, definitional and correct. Part 2 'high line burden INDEPENDENTLY raises the per-transition over-split rate beyond line decay' is inflated by endogeneity: the predictor (max cota_lot_numeric) is mechanically inflated by the over-splits being predicted (cota_tot = doctor_tot + n_over; repeat patients inflated +2.29 vs +1.0 lines). Using DOCTOR ground-truth total lines instead, the totlines logistic coef drops from +0.182 (p=4.6e-6) to +0.070 (p=0.16 NS), and the early-line stratified test drops from OR=1.87/p=0.052 to OR=1.34-1.52/p=0.24-0.35 (NS). The independent rate-elevation claim is NOT supported. Surviving: repeat offenders have more TRUE lines (median 9 vs 6, p=0.008), but this is opportunity (more transitions = more +1 chances), consistent with the report's own Poisson p=0.35.
verdict.recomputed: Canonical load reproduces (916=136 baseline+706 aligned+74 over-split, 136 patients). PART 1 atomic+1 EXACT: per-transition jump=+1 for 74/74; cota_inc=+1, doc_inc=0 (74/74); zero jumps>1. Cum shifts: +1=52,+2=17,+3=3,+4=1,+5=1. n_over==max cum shift for all 52 offenders (0 mismatches). 5x offender b739c87a-..., seq [1,2,3,4,5]. PART 2: repeat(17) vs single(35) COTA tot lines mean 10.41 vs 7.17, MWU p=0.0004; rate 24.4%(39/160) vs 16.2%(35/216). Logistic over~line+totlines: line -0.215, totlines +0.182, LR chi2=20.98 p=4.6e-6. Big vs +1 nulls reproduce: line 6.95 vs 3.44 (p=2e-6), drugs 2.77 vs 2.69 (p=0.83), no transplant enrichment. Early-line stratified Fisher COTA totlines>=8: 16.7%(23/138) vs 9.7%(25/259), OR=1.87, p=0.052 reproduce.
verdict.main_confound: Endogeneity: the 'independent total-line effect' uses COTA's own line count, which is arithmetically inflated by the over-splits being modeled (cota_tot = doctor_tot + n_over). Swapping in non-inflated doctor total lines makes the effect non-significant (logistic p 4.6e-6 to 0.16; Fisher p 0.052 to 0.24+).
verdict.critique: Part 1 is exact, novel, useful, reproduces to the digit. Part 2's causal claim of an independent line-burden effect is the flaw: COTA total lines is inflated by the very over-splits being predicted, guaranteeing a positive association regardless of truth. Corrected with doctor lines it vanishes; only opportunity plus a weak NS hint remains. Weakened not refuted because Part 1 is solid and 'repeat offenders more pretreated' holds on true lines (p=0.008), but as opportunity not a distinct driver. Subgroup tests underpowered (23-event cells), unadjusted for multiplicity.

raw_findings.title: Per-family over-split RATE (normalized by opportunity), not raw count

finding.claim: Transitions involving a Proteasome-inhibitor + Steroids (PI+Steroids) regimen — either before or after — are markedly PROTECTED against COTA over-splitting (4.2% vs 9.5% overall), and this protection survives controlling for line-number decay and exact-regimen-repeat confounds.
finding.evidence: Opportunity-normalized rate (over-splits where current OR previous reconstructed_family_combination == PI+Steroids, divided by all such transitions): 12/284 = 4.2% [Wilson 95% CI 2.4-7.2%] vs 62/496 = 12.5% for all other transitions; unadjusted Fisher OR=0.31, p=0.00011. This is the ONLY family combination (of 36 with n>=5) that passes Bonferroni (alpha=0.05/36=0.00139). Robustness: (1) PI+Steroids transitions sit at the SAME median line as overall (median line 5 vs 4; means 5.0 vs 5.1), so the known line-2-peak decay is not the cause; logistic is_over ~ line + pi_st gives adjusted OR=0.34. (2) The protection partly works by avoiding identical-regimen repeats (PI+Steroids repeats identically only 1.8% of the time vs 13.7% for others), but it is NOT fully explained by that: in a logistic controlling for BOTH line and same_drugs (exact-regimen-repeat), pi_st adjusted OR=0.40, LR-test chi2=7.61, p=0.0058. (3) Restricting to non-identical-regimen transitions only, PI+Steroids over-splits 9/279=3.2% vs 36/461=7.8% (OR=0.39, p=0.011). Secondary: the apparent high-rate families (Alkylating+PI+Transplant 33%, IMiDs+Transplant 33%) all have n_opp=6-10 and NONE survive testing (all p>0.10).
finding.effect_size: Rate ratio 0.45 (4.2% vs 9.5%); unadjusted OR=0.31 (p=0.00011); fully-adjusted OR=0.40 (for line + exact-repeat, LR p=0.0058). Direction: PI+Steroids reduces over-split odds ~60% per opportunity. Risk difference ~ -5.3 percentage points.
finding.sample_size: 780 transitions (74 over-split, 706 aligned). PI+Steroids opportunity set n=284 (12 over); non-PI+Steroids n=496 (62 over). 36 family combinations had n_opp>=5 and were tested; smaller ones dropped.
finding.caveats: Small absolute event count (12 over-splits in the PI+Steroids set). Protection is a NEGATIVE finding (a regimen type COTA handles WELL), which is the inverse of the assigned 'high-rate' hypothesis — the high-rate hypothesis is effectively a NULL: every family that LOOKED error-prone by raw rate (transplant/IMiDs combos at 25-33%) had n<=10 and failed significance, so raw-count leaders do not survive normalization in the dangerous direction. Part of PI+Steroids' protection operates through it rarely being repeated identically (a known over-split trigger); after removing that confound the effect shrinks (OR 0.31->0.40) but remains significant. 'OR previous' opportunity definition double-counts a transition under up to two families; I used clean() to strip the '(Not in provided Fiona's list)' suffix before grouping, which merges some borderline labels. Mechanism (why PI+Steroids specifically) is not established — likely it represents stable maintenance/continuation regimens COTA correctly does not re-line.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. Built prev_fam = within-patient shift(1) of reconstructed_family_combination. Restricted to TRANS (status != baseline_first_lot_row, n=780). is_over = (status==candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split). Cleaned family strings by stripping '(Not in provided...' suffix. For each family X with n_opp>=5: opportunity mask = (cur_f==X)|(prev_f==X); rate = over/n_opp; Wilson 95% CI; Fisher exact 2x2 (X vs all other transitions). Confound controls: (a) compared line distributions; (b) sklearn LogisticRegression (C=1e6) is_over ~ line + pi_st and ~ line + same_drugs + pi_st with manual log-likelihood LR chi2 tests (df=1); same_drugs = (parsed_drugs_repaired == within-patient prev parsed_drugs_repaired). Also tested same-family (prev_f==cur_f) vs changed-family, and family-transition pairs.
finding.secondary_observations: The same-FAMILY-repeated transition pattern (prev_family==cur_family) over-splits at 43.8% (32/73) vs 5.9% changed-family (OR=12.4, p<1e-9), BUT this is NOT novel: it is driven by identical drug sets (38/73 are exact-regimen repeats = the known same_exact_regimen_repeated label). When restricted to same-family-but-DIFFERENT-drugs, the effect disappears (8.6% vs 5.9%, p=0.46) — a useful null that bounds the known pattern. Highest-rate family transition PAIRS are all same-regimen self-loops (PI+Steroids->PI+Steroids 3/5, IMiDs+mAb+Steroids self 11/23, IMiDs+PI+Steroids self 9/24), confirming the over-split mechanism is dominated by COTA re-lining a continued/repeated regimen rather than any specific drug-family chemistry.

verdict.recomputed: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions (136 baseline + 706 aligned + 74 over-split = 916), built within-patient prev_f, restricted to 780 transitions. Core rate reproduces EXACTLY: PI+Steroids opportunity (cur OR prev == "Proteasome inhibitors + Steroids") = 12/284 = 4.23%, Wilson CI [2.43%, 7.24%]; other = 62/496 = 12.50%; overall = 9.49%; Fisher OR=0.309, p=0.000111. Bonferroni: 36 families with n_opp>=5 tested, alpha=0.00139; PI+Steroids is the ONLY one passing (next-smallest p=0.104). High-rate transplant families (33%) all have n=6-9 and p>0.10 - reproduced, they fail. Confound controls reproduce: logistic is_over~line+pi_st gives pi_st OR=0.31 (LR chi2=16.2 vs line-only); Mantel-Haenszel OR stratified by line = 0.334 (matches claimed 0.34); per-line stratification shows PI+Steroids lower at nearly every line (L2 .12 vs .15, L3 .06 vs .15, L4 .06 vs .12, L5 .00 vs .15, L6 .03 vs .13, L8 .00 vs .16). Exact-repeat control: logistic line+same_drugs+pi_st gives pi_st OR=0.399, LR chi2=7.61 p=0.0058 (exact match). Non-identical-regimen restriction: 9/279=3.2% vs 36/461=7.8%, OR=0.394, p=0.0112 (exact match). same_drugs strongly predicts over-split (72.5% vs 6.1%), confirming exact-repeat is a real confound that the analysis correctly removed.
verdict.corrected_effect: matches — core effect (4.2% vs 12.5% overall/9.5%, OR 0.31 unadjusted, 0.40 fully adjusted) is exactly right. One descriptive error in a caveat: PI+Steroids identical-repeat rate is 1.8% (5/284, correct) but the "others repeat 13.7%" figure is actually 7.1% (35/496) — does not affect the result, only the magnitude of one confound contrast. Added specificity finding: protection is PI-specific, not a generic "2-class steroid doublet" effect (IMiDs+Steroids OR=0.95 p=1.0, mAb+Steroids OR=1.29 p=0.50 are NOT protected), which strengthens rather than weakens the claim.
