verdict.main_confound: Exact-regimen-repeat (same_drugs) is the dominant confound — it predicts over-split at 72.5% vs 6.1%, and PI+Steroids rarely repeats identically (1.8%). The analysis correctly controls for it: after removing exact repeats AND the PI+Steroids->PI+Steroids self-loop (which over-splits at 60%, 3/5), protection persists at 3.2% vs 7.8% (OR 0.40, p=0.011). So the confound is real but does not explain away the effect. Residual: the effect shrinks from OR 0.31 to 0.40 after adjustment, so ~part of the headline protection runs through PI+Steroids being a non-repeated maintenance/continuation regimen.
verdict.critique: The finding survives adversarial attack. Arithmetic, denominators, control group (706 aligned), Bonferroni count, and all three confound controls reproduce to the digit. Caveats: (1) absolute event count is small (12 over-splits in the protected set; 9 after stripping repeats) so the adjusted CI is wide. (2) The "OR previous" opportunity definition double-counts the 5 self-loop transitions under both cur and prev — but decomposition shows enter-only=1.3%, exit-only=5.6%, both/self-loop=60%, so the protection is genuinely about entering/leaving PI+Steroids, and the dangerous self-loop direction is correctly excluded in robustness checks. (3) The protection generalizes partly to "contains PI" (OR 0.41, p=0.0006, n=588) but the PI+Steroids doublet is the cleanest signal; mechanism (stable continuation regimens COTA correctly does not re-line) is plausible but unestablished. (4) One mislabeled descriptive number (13.7% should be 7.1%) in a caveat — sloppy but immaterial. The high-rate hypothesis is correctly reported as effectively null. Overall a careful, honest, reproducible analysis.

finding.claim: Over-splits do NOT cluster in super-spreader patients: once you condition on each patient's number of transitions (exposure), the per-patient over-split counts are consistent with independent binomial sampling (in fact slightly under-dispersed), and no patient feature predicts the rate beyond exposure.
finding.evidence: 74 over-splits across 780 transitions in 136 patients (52 patients have >=1 over-split; count distribution: 84 patients=0, 35=1, 14=2, 2=3, 1=5). Global per-transition over-split rate p=0.0949. Exposure-conditioned binomial dispersion test: T=sum((obs-n_i*p)^2/(n_i*p*(1-p)))=114.3, df=135, dispersion ratio=0.847, p(overdispersion)=0.90, p(underdispersion)=0.10 -> NO overdispersion (if anything mild under). The naive marginal Poisson VMR=1.276 (var=0.694/mean=0.544) is only borderline (parametric-bootstrap p=0.056) and is an artifact of exposure heterogeneity: under a binomial(n_trans_i, p) null the bootstrap mean VMR is already 1.05 with 95% interval [0.82,1.34], covering the observed 1.276. The 'super-spreaders' are expected sampling extremes: observed max=5 vs H0 expected max=3.4 (p=0.073); observed #patients with >=3 over-splits=3 vs expected 2.85 (p=0.55); >=2 over-splits observed=17 vs expected 14.4 (p=0.26). Predictors: transplant per-transition OR=0.999, Fisher p=1.0 (30/316 non-tx vs 44/464 tx); standardized per-transition logistic over~lot+transplant+mean_drugs gives coefs lot=-0.27, transplant=+0.02, mean_drugs=+0.10 (line number dominates, patient features negligible). Count predictor max_lot is perfectly collinear with n_trans (Spearman r=1.0), so it is just exposure relabeled; low- vs high-exposure per-transition rates 0.072 vs 0.107 do not differ (Fisher p=0.13).
finding.effect_size: Exposure-conditioned dispersion ratio = 0.847 (95% under Poisson would be ~1.0; values <1 = under-dispersion), i.e. NO super-spreader inflation. Marginal VMR=1.28 but its excess over 1.0 is fully explained by exposure heterogeneity (bootstrap-expected VMR 1.05, obs inside the H0 95% interval). Transplant effect on over-split rate: OR=1.00 (null).
finding.sample_size: 74 over-splits vs 706 aligned among 780 transitions; 136 patients (52 with >=1 over-split, max 5 in one patient). Per-patient binomial test n=136; transplant crosstab n=780 transitions.
finding.caveats: Small dataset (n=74 events, 136 patients) gives limited power to detect mild true overdispersion, so 'no clustering' is 'no DETECTABLE clustering beyond exposure'; but the point estimate runs the opposite way (under-dispersion), which is reassuring against a missed-power story. The marginal Poisson dispersion test (p=0.017) and marginal VMR (p=0.056) would FALSELY suggest clustering if exposure is ignored - that mis-specified test is the trap. Feature definitions are heuristic: transplant flagged via regimen-string keywords (transplant/CAR-T/cell therapy/melphalan); regimen complexity = mean drug count parsed from line_of_therapy_name. The chi-square dispersion approximation is rough at small per-patient expected counts; the parametric bootstrap (20k draws) corroborates it. Patients with a single transition can only have rate 0 or 1, which inflates naive rate-vs-exposure Spearman (0.30) - that correlation is an artifact, not evidence of clustering.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. TRANS = non-baseline rows (780); is_over = candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split. Per patient computed n_trans (exposure) and n_over. (1) Marginal Poisson check: VMR=var/mean and chi2 dispersion. (2) Exposure-conditioned test: under H0 n_over_i ~ Binomial(n_trans_i, p_global), p_global=74/780; statistic T=sum((obs-exp)^2/(n_i p (1-p))) compared to chi2(N-1). (3) Parametric bootstrap (20,000 draws of Binomial(n_trans_i,p)) for null distributions of VMR, max count, #patients>=2 and >=3. (4) Predictors: per-transition Fisher exact for transplant x is_over; standardized sklearn LogisticRegression of is_over on lot, transplant, mean_drugs; Spearman of n_over and rate vs n_trans and max_lot; low/high-exposure split (median n_trans=5) Fisher test. Transplant and complexity built as patient-level keyword/parse features.
finding.secondary_observations: max_lot (total lines) and n_trans are perfectly collinear (Spearman r=1.0) in this data, so 'patients with more lines have more errors' is purely an exposure/denominator effect, not a complexity effect - any future claim that 'high-line patients are error-prone' on a count basis is a denominator artifact. The per-transition over-split rate does NOT rise with patient exposure (0.072 low vs 0.107 high, p=0.13), consistent with errors being a fixed-probability per-transition event. In the standardized per-transition logistic, line number (lot, coef -0.27) is by far the strongest signal - reaffirming the known line-2-peak decay curve as the dominant driver, while patient-level identity contributes essentially nothing beyond it.

verdict.recomputed: I independently reran everything in Python on All_COTA_With_Transitions (sorted cpid/_original_row_order, non-baseline = 780 transitions). Reproduced: 780 transitions, 74 over, 136 patients (all have >=1 transition), 52 with >=1 over-split, count distribution {0:84,1:35,2:14,3:2,5:1}, p_global=0.0949. Marginal Poisson: mean=0.5441, var=0.6943, VMR=1.2761, chi2 dispersion T=172.27/df135, ratio=1.276, p(over)=0.0167 (matches the 'trap' marginal test). Exposure-conditioned binomial dispersion: T=114.32, df=135, ratio=0.8468, p(over)=0.901, p(under)=0.099 -> no overdispersion, mild under. Parametric bootstrap (20k, Binomial(n_i,p)): VMR null mean=1.048, 95% CI [0.816,1.347] covering obs 1.276 (p=0.056); max obs=5 vs E=3.41 (p=0.072); #>=2 obs=17 vs E=14.4 (p=0.26); #>=3 obs=3 vs E=2.85 (p=0.55). Transplant (patient-level ever-tx propagated): 286/30 non-tx vs 420/44 tx = 316/464 split, Fisher OR=0.999, p=1.0 (exact match). Exposure split (median n_trans=5): low rate 0.072 vs high 0.107, Fisher p=0.126. Spearman max_lot vs n_trans = 1.0 (perfect collinearity). Standardized logistic over~lot+transplant+mean_drugs: lot=-0.27, transplant=-0.01, mean_drugs=+0.13. Every headline number reproduced within rounding.
verdict.corrected_effect: matches. Exposure-conditioned dispersion ratio 0.847 (no super-spreader inflation; mild under-dispersion), marginal VMR 1.28 fully explained by exposure heterogeneity (bootstrap-expected 1.05, obs inside H0 95% CI), transplant OR=1.00. One framing note, not a correction: the transplant null (OR=1.0) is the patient-level ever-transplant definition, which is the right framing for a patient-clustering question. A row-level 'is this regimen a transplant row' flag gives OR=2.13, p=0.08 (borderline) -- but that is a transition-level property, not patient clustering, so it does not weaken the super-spreader null; if anything it shows the only transplant signal lives at the transition level, consistent with the claim.
verdict.main_confound: Exposure heterogeneity (line-number / number-of-transitions per patient) is the obvious confound, and the analysis correctly identifies and neutralizes it: the marginal Poisson signal (VMR p=0.056, chi2 p=0.017) is the mis-specified trap, and conditioning on exposure removes it (ratio 1.276->0.847). No residual confound found. Power is the only real limitation (n=74 events), but the point estimate runs toward under-dispersion, so a missed-overdispersion story is implausible.
verdict.critique: The claim is a careful, correctly-executed null result. The core inferential move -- compare per-patient counts against an exposure-conditioned Binomial(n_i, p) null rather than a marginal Poisson -- is exactly right, and both the chi-square dispersion stat and an independent 20k parametric bootstrap agree the observed spread is within the binomial null. The 'super-spreader' (max=5) patient is an expected sampling extreme (p=0.072), not evidence of clustering. Minor quibbles: (1) transplant is defined as patient-level ever-tx via regimen-string keywords; a row-level flag yields a borderline OR=2.1 (p=0.08), but that is transition-level, not patient-level, so it does not rescue clustering -- the colleague could have stated this contrast to preempt the objection. (2) The chi-square dispersion approximation is rough at small per-patient expected counts, but the bootstrap correctly backstops it. (3) Honest about limited power. The confidence='high' is justified for 'no DETECTABLE clustering beyond exposure'.

raw_findings.title: Regimen structural complexity (multi-phase / drug-count / length) vs over-split

finding.claim: A multi-phase PREVIOUS regimen is the strongest structural predictor of a COTA over-split, but only at relapsed transitions (prev line >= 2): there the over-split rate is 4x higher when the regimen COTA is leaving had bracketed sub-phases (induction/maintenance structure), whereas at the first-line transition that same structure is mildly protective.
finding.evidence: Among 644 relapsed transitions (prev_cota_lot >= 2): over-split rate = 31/157 (19.7%) when the previous regimen was multi-phase (>1 bracket) vs 24/487 (4.9%) when single-phase; rate ratio 4.01, Fisher OR=4.75, RR(of multiphase share)=2.63, p=9.5e-08. Among OVER relapsed transitions, 56% (31/55) had a multi-phase previous regimen vs 21% (126/589) of ALIGN. At the L1->L2 transition (n=136) the direction reverses: multi-phase prev over-split 7/79 (8.9%) vs single-phase 12/57 (21.1%) (Fisher OR=0.36, p=0.049). Logistic is_over ~ prev_multiphase * relapsed: prev_multiphase main OR=0.36, interaction OR=13.0; LRT for interaction chi2=19.54, p<0.0001. Marginal (unstratified) prev_multiphase: OVER 38/74 (51.4%) vs ALIGN 198/706 (28.0%), OR=2.71, p=1e-04, bootstrap 95% CI [1.67, 4.54]. CURRENT-regimen multiphase was NOT significant (OVER 29.7% vs ALIGN 21.7%, OR=1.53, p=0.14).
finding.effect_size: Relapsed stratum: rate ratio ~4.0 (19.7% vs 4.9%), Fisher OR=4.75. Interaction OR=13.0 (multiphase flips from protective at L1 to strongly harmful at relapse). Mantel-Haenszel pooled OR across prev-line strata = 2.05 overall, 4.55 restricted to prev_line>=2.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 vs ALIGN n=706 (780 transitions). Relapsed subgroup (prev_line>=2): n=644 transitions, 55 over-splits. L1->L2 subgroup: n=136, 19 over-splits. Multiphase-prev relapsed cell n=157.
finding.caveats: The protective-then-harmful interaction rests on the small L1 stratum (only 19 over-splits, 7 in the multiphase cell), so the reversal direction is plausible but the L1 OR=0.36 (p=0.049) is borderline. prev_multiphase is itself correlated with line number (multiphase rate falls from 58% at L1 to ~10-18% at L4+), but the signal survives line-number adjustment (logistic prev_multiphase OR=2.51 with prev_line in the model) and the Mantel-Haenszel pooling, so it is not merely the known line-decay confound. Multi-phase here means COTA emitted >1 bracketed group within a single doctor line (e.g. [carfilzomib,daratumumab,dex],[daratumumab]) -- this overlaps mechanistically with the known drug-drop/de-escalation subset, since the trailing bracket is usually a reduced maintenance phase; the structural feature may be an alternative encoding of that pattern rather than fully independent of it. Per-transition rows are not independent within patient (136 patients); no patient-cluster correction applied.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, stripped cols, sorted by cpid,_original_row_order. Parsed line_of_therapy_name into bracket phases via regex \[([^\]]*)\]; phase count = number of bracket groups (1 if none), multiphase = phases>1; total/unique drug counts from comma-split within brackets. Built prev_lot_name = groupby(cpid).shift(1) and parsed identically for the PREVIOUS regimen. Restricted to transitions (status != baseline_first_lot_row): OVER = candidate_misclassification_cota_over_split (74), ALIGN = transition_aligned (706). Tests: Mann-Whitney U for continuous (phases/drug counts), Fisher exact for multiphase 2x2. Confound control: line number = previous_cota_lot_numeric; (a) logistic is_over ~ prev_multiphase + prev_line(std) [sklearn, C=1e6/penalty=None]; (b) stratified Fisher by prev_line; (c) Mantel-Haenszel pooled OR; (d) logistic with prev_multiphase*relapsed interaction (relapsed = prev_line>=2) plus likelihood-ratio test vs no-interaction model. Bootstrap (5000 resamples, seed=1) for the marginal OR CI.
finding.secondary_observations: prev_totaldrugs is also higher in OVER (median 3.5 vs 3.0, MWU p=0.002) and cur_totaldrugs/cur_uniqdrugs are mildly elevated (p~0.01), but these are weaker and partly track the multiphase signal. The key asymmetry is PREVIOUS structure mattering far more than CURRENT structure, consistent with the known directionality that over-splits are de-escalations away from a complex multi-phase regimen: COTA reads the trailing maintenance bracket of the prior line as the start of a new line. prev_phases distribution among OVER is concentrated at exactly 2 brackets (31/74) and 3 (7), never the very long 5-8 bracket chains seen only in ALIGN -- so it is 2-3 phase induction+maintenance structures, not extreme multi-phase regimens, that drive the error.

verdict.recomputed: Re-loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions (74 over / 706 align / 136 baseline, matches). Parsed bracket phases via regex, built prev_lot_name = groupby(cpid).shift(1). Reproduced EVERY headline number: marginal prev_multiphase OVER 38/74 (51.4%) vs ALIGN 198/706 (28.0%), Fisher OR=2.708, p=8.70e-5. Relapsed (prev_line>=2): 31/157 (19.7%) vs 24/487 (4.9%), RR=4.007, Fisher OR=4.746, p=9.54e-8; OVER-relapsed multiphase share 56.4%. L1->L2 reversal: 7/79 (8.9%) vs 12/57 (21.1%), Fisher OR=0.365, p=0.049. Line-adjusted logistic prev_multiphase OR=2.512. Interaction model: main OR=0.365, interaction OR=13.02, LRT chi2=19.54 (p=9.9e-6, consistent with their <0.0001). Current-multiphase OR=1.529, p=0.142 (NS), matches. MH pooled: I got 1.95 overall and 4.07 for prev>=2 (they reported 2.05 and 4.55 — minor weighting difference, same conclusion). ADVERSARIAL TESTS I added: (1) de-escalation confound — among 38 OVER multiphase rows only 10 are de-escalations; logistic with deescal+prev_line controlled keeps prev_multiphase OR=1.96; restricting to relapsed NON-de-escalation rows prev_multiphase still gives 21/140 (15.0%) vs 20/482 (4.1%), Fisher OR=4.08, p=4.8e-5, so the signal is NOT just the known drug-drop pattern. (2) Patient-cluster bootstrap (not done by authors): marginal OR 95% CI [1.58, 4.90], still excludes 1; their row-bootstrap CI [1.67,4.54] reproduces as [1.63,4.48]. (3) prev_phases among OVER = {1:36, 2:31, 3:7}, max 8 only in ALIGN — confirms 2-3 phase structures drive it.
verdict.corrected_effect: Matches. Relapsed-stratum rate ratio ~4.0 (19.7% vs 4.9%), Fisher OR=4.75, line-adjusted OR=2.5 all reproduced. Minor nits: MH pooled OR is ~1.95/4.07 in my run vs their 2.05/4.55 (different stratum handling); LRT p is 9.9e-6 vs their <0.0001 — neither changes the conclusion. The de-escalation-independence is actually STRONGER than the authors claimed: their caveat treats the structural feature as possibly an alternative encoding of de-escalation, but restricting to non-de-escalation relapsed rows still yields OR=4.08 (p=4.8e-5), so it is a genuinely distinct predictor, not a re-encoding.
verdict.main_confound: Line number (prev_multiphase correlates with line) and overlap with the known de-escalation/drug-drop subset. I tested both directly: the signal survives line-number adjustment (OR 2.51) and survives removal of de-escalation rows (relapsed non-deescal OR 4.08, p=4.8e-5). Residual concern is per-row non-independence within 136 patients, which the authors did not correct; my added patient-cluster bootstrap CI [1.58,4.90] still excludes 1, so clustering does not overturn it.
verdict.critique: Numbers are honest and reproduce to the digit; no cherry-picking or miscomputation. The strongest part (relapsed effect, marginal effect, current-vs-previous asymmetry, line-confound robustness) is solid. The weakest claim is the L1->L2 REVERSAL ("mildly protective at first line"): it rests on 7 over-splits in the multiphase cell with p=0.049 (borderline), and the interaction OR=13 is leveraged by that tiny stratum — authors flag this themselves. The phrase "strongest structural predictor" is defensible, but de-escalation as a behavioral feature is actually stronger when co-modeled (logistic OR ~4.6 vs 2.0). The authors' caveat that multiphase might just re-encode de-escalation is overly modest — my non-deescal test shows it is independent. Net: claim holds.

raw_findings.title: Wildcard / completeness critic: anything the other angles miss

finding.claim: COTA over-splits are driven by the bracket-PHASE structure of the PREVIOUS line: when the prior regimen is multi-phase (an induction phase followed by a maintenance/de-escalation phase, >=2 bracket groups), the next transition is ~2.4x more likely to be a COTA over-split, and the mechanism is COTA re-counting the induction drug set as a brand-new line after the maintenance phase ends.
finding.evidence: Previous line being multi-phase (>=2 bracket groups in line_of_therapy_name): OVER 38/74 = 51.4% vs ALIGN 198/706 = 28.0% (Fisher OR 2.71, p=8.7e-5). Phase-DROP (current has fewer bracket phases than previous) is also enriched: OVER 32/74=43.2% vs ALIGN 166/706=23.5% (OR 2.48, p=4.0e-4). Adjusting for COTA line number in a logistic model, prev-multi-phase keeps adjusted OR=2.37 (per-line OR 0.95, the known decay). Stratified: L3-4 prev-multi 18.9%(n=95) vs prev-single 6.6%(n=166); L5+ prev-multi 21.0%(n=62) vs single 4.0%(n=321) — effect holds and grows in later lines (L2 reverses: 8.9% vs 21.1%). Mechanism: of the 38 prev-multi-phase over-splits, 25 (66%) have a current drug set exactly equal to the FIRST/induction bracket of the prior multi-phase line; that is 34% of all 74 over-splits. Separately, 24/74 (32.4%) over-splits have an IDENTICAL parsed drug SET to the previous row but a DIFFERENT regimen name string (a pure phase-structure/parsing artifact) vs only 10/706 (1.4%) of aligned (the same-drug-set-overall RR is 23.9, p=2e-24).
finding.effect_size: Unadjusted OR 2.71 (rate ratio 1.84: 51.4% vs 28.0%); line-number-adjusted OR 2.37. Phase-drop OR 2.48. Within-stratum risk differences: L5+ +17.0 pts, L3-4 +12.3 pts.
finding.sample_size: OVER n=74 vs ALIGN n=706 (780 transitions). Prev-multi-phase subgroup: 38 OVER, 198 ALIGN. Induction-match subgroup n=25. Logistic on 780 transitions with non-null prev phase count and line number.
finding.caveats: Overlaps mechanistically with the known subset/de-escalation and same-exact-regimen sub-patterns — the novelty is reframing them as a PREVIOUS-LINE phase-structure (induction+maintenance) trigger, not a property of the current row, and quantifying it against the ALIGN control. The L2 stratum reverses direction (prev-multi LOWER rate, 8.9% vs 21.1%), so prev-multi-phase is not a uniform predictor across line number; the signal is concentrated in lines >=3, and small per-stratum n's (L3-4 prev-single n=166, L5+ prev-single n=321) keep individual strata noisy. Phase count is parsed by counting '[' in line_of_therapy_name, so it is sensitive to COTA's own bracket formatting (which is partly what we are critiquing). n=74 over-splits overall warrants humility.
finding.method: Loaded All_COTA_With_Transitions, sorted by cpid/_original_row_order. Defined phase count = number of '[' bracket groups in line_of_therapy_name; previous-row values via groupby(cpid).shift(1). prev_multi = (prev phase count >=2). Compared prev_multi rate OVER vs ALIGN with scipy.stats.fisher_exact; computed phase-drop = (cur phases < prev phases). Ran sklearn LogisticRegression of over ~ prev_multi + cota_lot_numeric on the 780 transitions to control for the known line-number decay; reported exp(coef) as adjusted ORs and computed raw over-rates within line strata L2 / L3-4 / L5+. For the induction-match mechanism, parsed each line's bracket groups into drug sets and tested whether the current row's full drug set equals the prior multi-phase line's first (induction) bracket. Also computed same-drug-SET (parsed_drugs_repaired tokenized on ,[];/) vs same-NAME equality to isolate the phase-structure/parsing-artifact slice.
finding.secondary_observations: Null/checked-and-clean wildcard angles: (1) reviewer identity has no effect — over-split rate is uniform across Reviewer 1 persons (8.0-13.3%) and Reviewer 2 persons (7.4-11.4%); the two reviewer LoT columns disagree on only 4/916 rows and 0/74 OVER rows, so reviewer disagreement is not the source. (2) Line durations are null: current-line duration MWU p=0.43, previous-line duration MWU p=0.23, and very-short-line fractions are not elevated in OVER. (3) Date gaps between prev-end and current-start are similar (median 17 vs 21 days) and date overlaps are not enriched in OVER (6/74 vs 41/706). Reviewer 2 LoT column is entirely empty (0/916).

verdict.recomputed: Reproduced all primary numbers exactly. prev_multi (prev line has >=2 bracket groups): OVER 38/74=51.4% vs ALIGN 198/706=28.0%, Fisher OR 2.708, p=8.7e-5 (matches). Phase-drop: OVER 32/74=43.2% vs 166/706=23.5%, OR 2.478, p=4.0e-4 (matches). Per-line decay OR 0.952 (matches). Strata reproduce: L2 reverses (8.9% n=79 vs 21.1% n=57), L3-4 18.9% vs 6.6%, L5+ 21.0% vs 4.0%. Induction-match mechanism 25/38=66%, 34% of 74 (matches). same_set_diff_name 24/74=32.4% vs 10/706=1.4% (matches); same_set RR 23.9 (matches). My logistic adj OR for prev_multi was 2.51 (they said 2.37 — minor, both substantial). CRITICAL re-computation they omitted: controlling for same_set (current drug set identical to previous row) in logistic over~prev_multi+same_set+line, prev_multi adj OR COLLAPSES to 1.12 while same_set OR=36.8. Within non-same-set transitions prev_multi is null (7.4% n=203 vs 5.4% n=535, OR 1.39, p=0.30). Within prev_single transitions same_set remains overwhelming (77.8% vs 5.4%, OR 61, p=1e-7). Of the 38 prev_multi over-splits, 23 are same_set; only 15 are not, and those 15 are not elevated above baseline.
verdict.corrected_effect: The real driver is "current row has the SAME parsed drug SET as the previous row" (a same-regimen-repeat / phase-parsing artifact): OVER 30/74=40.5% vs ALIGN 12/706=1.7%, OR ~39, p=2e-24. The headline "previous-line is multi-phase" effect (unadjusted OR 2.71) is largely a CONFOUND of same_set: its adjusted OR drops to ~1.1 once same_set is held fixed, and it carries no significant signal among non-same-set transitions (OR 1.39, p=0.30). So the framing should be reversed: it is not the prior line's induction+maintenance phase structure per se, but the current line repeating the prior drug set, that triggers over-splits. prev-multi-phase is a weak correlate, not the mechanism.
verdict.main_confound: same_set (current drug set identical to previous row). prev-multi-phase rides on it: prev_multi adjusted OR falls 2.51 -> 1.12 once same_set is controlled, and prev_multi is non-significant (p=0.30) within non-same-set transitions, while same_set stays OR=61 (p=1e-7) within prev_single transitions.
verdict.critique: The arithmetic, denominators, and control group are all correct and reproduce, and the caveats honestly flag overlap with same-regimen/de-escalation patterns plus the L2 reversal. But the finding stops one regression short: it never pits prev_multi against same_set head-to-head. When you do, prev_multi is exposed as a downstream correlate, not a driver — multi-phase prior lines simply tend to be followed by a row repeating the (induction) drug set, and it is that repeat that COTA over-counts. The genuinely strong, novel-against-control result here is the same-drug-set-vs-control signal (OR ~39, RR 23.9), which is real and large; the "previous-line phase structure / induction re-count mechanism" superstructure built on top of it is the part that does not survive adjustment. Hence weakened, not refuted: a real artifact is found, but the proposed causal framing is wrong and its independent effect size is ~null.
